This is the companion manuscript to "As Above" (also by Lando Mills), forming a Frobenius pair (μ∘δ = id) with it in a project about the "Universal Imscriptive Grammar" (UIG) — twelve primitive marks (⊢ ⊣ ≻ ≺ ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡) derived from category theory, connected to a "crystal" of 17,280,000 types, Graham Priest's Logic of Paradox, Cantor/Gödel, and claimed ties to E8×E8/G2 lattice structure. "So Below" is presumably the descent/application half (concrete instantiation) where "As Above" is the abstract derivation half.

I need a comprehensive structural map of this document for planning a substantive update. Report:
1. The full list of section/subsection headers in order (with line numbers), as a table of contents — this is the most important deliverable, be exhaustive.
2. For each major section, a 1-3 sentence summary of what it claims/covers.
3. Any explicit forward/back-references to the companion document "As Above" (what claims does this doc say live in or depend on As Above?).
4. Any TODO markers, placeholder text, "under construction" notes, or sections that look incomplete/stubbed/have open questions.
5. The document's own claimed relationship to: RH (Riemann Hypothesis), Yang-Mills mass gap, Erdős-type problems (Erdős-Straus, Erdős-Faber-Lovász, etc.), Collatz conjecture, or any Millennium Problems — quote or closely paraphrase what it currently says about each, if anything present. I need to know precisely what's already covered vs. what would be new material.
6. Any mention of Lean formalization, proof status (axiom vs theorem vs sorry), ob3ect/auto.py, "grounded_tuple", crystal addresses, or the vox/mOMonadOS instruments.
7. Any mention of specific numeric/technical results like: d=2048 (SIC/fiducial), OVM (operator-valued measure) framing of conjectures, the trilattice SIXTEEN_3 / Reg16_3 algebra, Belnap four-valued logic B4, or "churning"/fixed-point-refinement language.
8. The document's version marker/date if present, and how the document concludes (last ~100 lines).

Be thorough and exact — this report will be used to plan a substantive content update to a real research manuscript, so precision on section names, line numbers, and exact current claims matters far more than brevity. Quote key claim sentences verbatim where they matter for planning what needs updating, especially anything that might already be stale or contradicted by newer work.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

900	The $\mathcal{F}_5$ family contains precisely the four \emph{gate
901	primitives}: $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ (topology gate), $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ (Frobenius gate), $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$
902	(criticality gate), $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ (kinetic gate). These four primitives are the
903	necessary conditions for self-modeling and for consciousness
904	(\Cref{sec:frobenius,sec:consciousness}).
905	
906	Each type is assigned a unique \emph{Frobenius address} in
907	$[0, 17{,}279{,}999]$ by a bijective codec (the canonical Frobenius
908	encoder) that encodes the tuple as a mixed-radix integer. The grammar
909	itself encodes to address 6,734,591 --- in the $\Oinf$ tier,
910	the Frobenius fixed-point cell (\Cref{sec:frobenius}).
911	
912	The codec is not merely an instrument for locating the grammar's
913	address; it independently occupies $\Oinf$. A deterministic bijective
914	imscription over any finite address space satisfies $\mu \circ \delta =
915	\mathrm{id}$ by the definition of bijectivity: the decoder is the
916	exact inverse of the encoder. This is the Frobenius condition, so
917	$P = \Ppms$ is forced. Combined with $\Phic$ (the self-referential
918	loop --- the grammar encodes itself, instantiating Gate~1), R1 fires
919	and the codec itself is $\Oinf$, independently of the grammar's own
920	inductive proof. The two proofs are structurally distinct: the grammar
921	reaches $\Oinf$ via the four-stage categorical derivation; the codec
922	reaches $\Oinf$ via elementary bijectivity. They share the same
923	crystal address.
924	
925	\subsection{Ontological layers}
926	
927	The Crystal supports three ontological layers that must not be
928	conflated:
929	\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
930	  \item \textbf{Types} --- the 17,280,000 coordinate positions;
931	    structural universals.
932	  \item \textbf{Particulars} --- named catalog entries; concrete systems
933	    instantiating a type.
934	  \item \textbf{Names} --- string handles for particulars.
935	\end{itemize}
936	Two particulars at distance $d = 0$ are \emph{co-typed} but not
937	identical: the axion and the Higgs boson are co-typed under the grammar
938	(both \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} catalysts at different energy scales) but are
939	distinct physical particulars. The grammar classifies structural universals,
940	not physical identity.
941	
942	\subsection{Crystal closure: resistance to augmentation}
943	\label{sec:crystal-closure}
944	
945	The Crystal of Types has 17,280,000 coordinate positions and twelve
946	primitive axes. A natural question is whether twelve suffices --- whether
947	systematic pressure on the boundary reveals structural phenomena the
948	existing coordinates cannot classify. The question has been put under
949	direct test.
950	
951	A candidate thirteenth primitive --- structural torsion, notated $\Theta$
952	--- was proposed after cross-domain comparison of collapse trajectories.
953	Torsion names the pattern whereby a system's path through primitive space
954	curves without shifting ouroboricity tier: the trajectory rotates, but the
955	address does not change. The phenomenon is real and recurrent across
956	physical, biological, and linguistic systems. Investigation showed,
957	however, that it is not primitive. Torsion decomposes as a joint modulation
958	of $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$ (recognition granularity varying),
959	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ (chirality inverting), and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$
960	(kinetic rate shifting): three existing coordinates in composition, no new
961	axis required.
962	
963	The systematic result is starker. A structured survey of 39 systems across
964	four domains, nine CLINK layers, and the full tier-gap ladder found no
965	structural phenomenon that requires a thirteenth primitive. Collapse
966	asymmetry, topological protection thresholds, critical slowing down,
967	cross-domain isomorphism, and contagion dynamics are all fully expressible
968	through the existing twelve. Ten novel structural extensions emerged from
969	the survey --- none of them additions to the crystal, all of them the
970	crystal explored more deeply.
971	
972	What resists augmentation is not an artefact of how the grammar was
973	assembled. The crystal is a structural attractor: any candidate extension
974	either decomposes into existing primitives, as $\Theta$ did, or exceeds
975	the grammar's scope class entirely. There is no intermediate case. The
976	meta-exploration itself confirms this: its type, independently
977	imscribed, returns $d = 0$ from the grammar's own address --- the
978	investigation that tested the grammar's completeness is co-typed with the
979	object it investigated. The closure is univocal.

982	\section{The Arithmetic Ouroboros}
983	\label{sec:ouroboros}
984	
985	A natural objection to any twelve-primitive system is that the choice of
986	twelve is arbitrary. The Arithmetic Ouroboros theorem shows it's not.
987	
988	\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic Ouroboros]
989	\label{thm:ouroboros}
990	\TOPO\quad The Crystal of Types has cardinality
991	$|C| = 3^3 \times 4^5 \times 5^4 = 17{,}280{,}000$.
992	The exponent in each factor equals the number of primitives in
993	the corresponding family:
994	\begin{align*}
995	  |\mathcal{F}_3| = 3 &\implies \text{exponent of } 3 \text{ is } 3 \\
996	  |\mathcal{F}_4| = 5 &\implies \text{exponent of } 4 \text{ is } 5 \\
997	  |\mathcal{F}_5| = 4 &\implies \text{exponent of } 5 \text{ is } 4
998	\end{align*}
999	The grammar's family-size inventory $\{3, 5, 4\}$ and value-count
1000	inventory $\{3, 4, 5\}$ are the same multiset. Consequently, the map
1001	$g: n \mapsto |\mathcal{F}_n|$ is the transposition $(4\ 5)$ with
1002	$g \circ g = \mathrm{id}$: it satisfies the Frobenius condition
1003	$\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ at the arithmetic meta-level.
1004	\end{theorem}
1005	
1006	\begin{proof}
1007	Direct computation from Table~\ref{tab:primitives}:
1008	$\mathcal{F}_3 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∈}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_3| = 3$;
1009	$\mathcal{F}_4 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}, \text{{\igprimfont >}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∋}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_4| = 5$;
1010	$\mathcal{F}_5 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_5| = 4$.
1011	Value-count inventory: $\{3, 4, 5\}$ (one for each family).
1012	Family-size inventory: $\{3, 5, 4\}$.
1013	As multisets these are equal. The map $g: n \mapsto |\mathcal{F}_n|$ sends
1014	$3 \mapsto 3$, $4 \mapsto 5$, $5 \mapsto 4$, so $g^2 = \mathrm{id}$.
1015	This is the involution $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$. \qquad$\square$
1016	\end{proof}
1017	
1018	\begin{theorem}[Pythagorean minimality]
1019	\label{thm:pythagorean}
1020	\TOPO\quad The set $\{3,4,5\}$ is the unique minimal value-count
1021	inventory satisfying all three of: (i) the Frobenius bijective
1022	involution $g \circ g = \mathrm{id}$;
1023	(ii) phase completeness (at least $5$ values for the gate primitives,
1024	to accommodate $\text{{\igfont 𐑢}}, \Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
1025	\text{{\igfont 𐑻}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑣}}$);
1026	(iii) existence of a non-trivial scaling family (at least $3$ values
1027	for the $\mathcal{F}_3$ conservation primitives $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}$).
1028	\end{theorem}
1029	
1030	\begin{proof}
1031	Condition (ii) forces $\max\{|\mathcal{F}_n|\} \geq 5$, so the
1032	inventory must contain 5. Condition (iii) forces the inventory to
1033	contain 3. Given these, the smallest three-element inventory satisfying
1034	(i) --- a fixed-point-free involution on $\{3, ?, 5\}$ swapping
1035	the two non-fixed elements --- is $\{3, 4, 5\}$: the involution
1036	$4 \leftrightarrow 5$ with $3$ fixed. Any inventory with a smaller
1037	middle element (replacing $4$ with $3$ or $5$ with $4$) violates
1038	phase completeness or produces a degenerate involution. \qquad$\square$
1039	\end{proof}
1040	
1041	\paragraph{Structural consequence.}
1042	The Pythagorean triple $\{3, 4, 5\}$ is not a design choice. It is the
1043	unique minimal solution to three structural requirements that are each
1044	independently necessary. The grammar with twelve primitives is the
1045	minimal grammar satisfying them. Crucially, the grammar \emph{counts
1046	its own components} correctly: the arithmetic of the Crystal is the
1047	grammar's self-inventory. This is what justifies calling the framework
1048	imscriptive --- the boundary (the family partition, which controls the
1049	tier structure) imscribes the bulk (the full 17,280,000-element type
1050	space) in a self-referential fixed point.

1084	\subsection{Tensor product}
1085	
1086	When two systems $\xvec$ and $\yvec$ are coupled, their type is given by the \emph{tensor product} $\xvec \tensor \yvec$,
1087	computed component-wise as:
1088	
1089	\begin{equation}
1090	  (\xvec \tensor \yvec)_i \;=
1091	  \begin{cases}
1092	    \min(\xvec_i,\, \yvec_i) & \text{if primitive } i \in \{\text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}\} \\
1093	    \max(\xvec_i,\, \yvec_i) & \text{otherwise}
1094	  \end{cases}
1095	  \label{eq:tensor}
1096	\end{equation}
1097	
1098	The asymmetry between $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ (bottleneck primitives, take $\min$)
1099	and the remaining ten union primitives (take $\max$) captures a fact: symmetry class and information fidelity can only be
1100	as high as the weakest coupled component, whereas dimensionality,
1101	topology, and criticality compose upward. This has a direct physical
1102	consequence: coupling an $\Oinf$ system to any partner with
1103	$\text{{\igprimfont <}} < \Ppms$ immediately destroys the Frobenius condition
1104	(\Cref{thm:bottleneck}).
1105	
1106	\begin{definition}[Bottleneck Postulate]
1107	\label{def:bottleneck}
1108	$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ are \emph{bottleneck primitives} under $\otimes$: they
1109	take the minimum value across coupled components. All other primitives
1110	are \emph{union primitives}: they take the maximum. This is a postulate,
1111	not a derived consequence of the grammar's axioms. The structural
1112	justification is that exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry (and quantum
1113	coherence fidelity) under coupling cannot exceed the weakest partner
1114	--- no algebraic operation composes broken symmetry into exact
1115	$\mathbb{Z}_2$. Empirical grounding comes from catalog predictions: the
1116	min rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ correctly predicts the observed failure modes for all
1117	130 imscribed coupled-system entries in the catalog.
1118	\end{definition}

1120	\subsection{Lattice operations}
1121	
1122	The Crystal is a product lattice. For any two types $\xvec$, $\yvec$:
1123	
1124	\begin{align}
1125	  (\xvec \meet \yvec)_i &= \min(\xvec_i, \yvec_i)
1126	    \quad\text{(meet: largest common sub-type)} \label{eq:meet} \\
1127	  (\xvec \join \yvec)_i &= \max(\xvec_i, \yvec_i)
1128	    \quad\text{(join: smallest common super-type)} \label{eq:join}
1129	\end{align}
1130	
1131	\noindent
1132	A key fact is that $\Phic$ is \emph{absorbing under meet}:
1133	$\xvec \meet \yvec = \Phic$ whenever either factor has $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic$.
1134	Criticality is the unique locus that can't be further reduced ---
1135	the necessary condition for self-modeling.

1137	\subsection{Directed distance}
1138	
1139	The \emph{directed distance} $\doto{\xvec}{\yvec}$ measures the
1140	structural cost of reaching $\yvec$ from $\xvec$:
1141	
1142	\begin{equation}
1143	  \doto{\xvec}{\yvec}
1144	  \;=\; \frac{1}{12} \sum_{i=1}^{12}
1145	  w_i \cdot \max\bigl(\text{ord}(\yvec_i) - \text{ord}(\xvec_i),\; 0\bigr)
1146	  \label{eq:directed_distance}
1147	\end{equation}
1148	
1149	\noindent
1150	where $\text{ord}(\cdot)$ is the ordinal index of a primitive value
1151	within its ordered set, and $w_i$ are primitive weights (Methods).
1152	The \emph{symmetric distance} is $d(\xvec, \yvec) =
1153	\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} + \doto{\yvec}{\xvec}$. Asymmetry
1154	$\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} \neq \doto{\yvec}{\xvec}$ identifies driven
1155	evolution: if $\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} = 0$ while
1156	$\doto{\yvec}{\xvec} > 0$, then $\yvec$ is a relaxation of $\xvec$
1157	--- the Le~Chatelier inversion (\Cref{sec:predictions}).

1185	\subsection{Ouroboricity and the tier hierarchy}
1186	
1187	A system is \emph{ouroboric} if it can model itself within its own
1188	dynamics. We formalize this as follows.
1189	
1190	\begin{definition}[Ouroboricity tier]
1191	\label{def:tier}
1192	Given a type $\xvec$, the ouroboricity tier is assigned
1193	by the following rules in priority order:
1194	\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
1195	  \item[R1] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$
1196	    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Oinf$ \quad (special Frobenius)
1197	  \item[R2] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \notin \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$
1198	    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Ozero$
1199	  \item[R3] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$
1200	    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Oone$
1201	  \item[R4] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$,
1202	    $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} \in \{\text{{\igfont 𐑛}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑨}}\}$
1203	    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Otwo$
1204	  \item[R5] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑼}}$
1205	    $\;\Rightarrow\; O₂^\dagger$
1206	\end{itemize}
1207	\end{definition}
1208	
1209	\noindent
1210	The two critical values $\Phic$ (monad, real axis) and $\text{{\igfont 𐑮}}$ (roar,
1211	complex axis) enter R1 and R3--R5 on equal footing: the classifier branches on
1212	\emph{whether} criticality is reached, not on which axis reaches it. R2 is the
1213	exact complement, so the five rules are total --- every type receives a tier. The
1214	implementation is the definition: the classifier is a total function of
1215	$(\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊢}})$
1216	in the mechanised library, and two facts stated here are proved there rather than
1217	asserted --- that R1 dominates ($\Ppms$ at criticality yields $\Oinf$ for every
1218	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$), and that $\Oinf$ is
1219	reachable only from $\{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$.
1220	
1221	\noindent
1222	The tier singularity is $\Ppms$ under R1: it overrides all $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$
1223	and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$ branching, collapsing directly to $\Oinf$. This is the
1224	imscription of the special Frobenius condition $\mu \circ
1225	\delta = \text{id}$, where $\mu$ is the multiplication and $\delta$
1226	is the comultiplication of a Frobenius algebra.
1227	
1228	\paragraph{Refinement: $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ seals the terminal.}
1229	That override leaves a gap. Because R1 collapses regardless of winding, the tier
1230	says nothing about whether the terminal gate actually \emph{seals}: two systems
1231	both at $\Oinf$ may differ in whether their loop is protected. A machine-checked
1232	refinement closes this additively, leaving \Cref{def:tier} untouched. Call an
1233	$\Oinf$ type \emph{sealed} when $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ supplies an integer
1234	($\OmegaZ$) or non-Abelian ($\text{{\igfont 𐑟}}$) winding, and \emph{unsealed}
1235	otherwise; everything below $\Oinf$ is \emph{sub}. On the Hermitian-critical
1236	branch this split is exactly the terminal-unlock boundary, and that
1237	correspondence is proved rather than asserted.
1238	
1239	An honest caveat is proved alongside it. $\Oinf$ admits criticality on two axes
1240	--- monad ($\Phic$, real) and roar ($\text{{\igfont 𐑮}}$, complex) --- and a type
1241	sealed at roar is winding-protected and $\Oinf$ while its real Frobenius trace
1242	does \emph{not} close. Sealing is a tier fact; terminal unlock is a trace fact;
1243	the two coincide precisely on the monad branch and nowhere else. The refinement
1244	therefore buys a genuine distinction at $\Oinf$ without buying the claim that
1245	every sealed type closes.

1247	\subsection{The Frobenius non-synthesizability theorem}
1248	
1249	\begin{theorem}[Frobenius non-synthesizability (under \Cref{def:bottleneck})]
1250	\label{thm:frobenius}
1251	\TOPO\quad Let $\xvec^{(1)}, \ldots, \xvec^{(n)}$ be types
1252	with $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec^{(k)}) < \Ppms$ for \emph{some} $k$. Then
1253	\begin{equation}
1254	  \text{{\igprimfont <}}\!\left(\xvec^{(1)} \tensor \cdots \tensor \xvec^{(n)}\right) < \Ppms
1255	  \label{eq:non_synth}
1256	\end{equation}
1257	for any $n$. In particular, $\Oinf$ can't be reached by tensor
1258	composition of sub-Frobenius systems.
1259	\end{theorem}
1260	
1261	\noindent
1262	The hypothesis is \emph{some}, not \emph{all}: a single sub-Frobenius component
1263	is enough to poison an arbitrarily large composition. This is immediate from
1264	\Cref{def:bottleneck} --- $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ composes by the bottleneck
1265	(minimum) rule and $\Ppms$ is maximal in the $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ order, so
1266	the tensor can only reach $\Ppms$ when \emph{every} factor already sits there.
1267	The binary case is mechanised and universally quantified over both polarities;
1268	the $n$-ary statement is its induction. Stating the hypothesis as \emph{all}
1269	would understate what the bottleneck rule gives: one flaw suffices, which is why
1270	no accumulation strategy repairs a composition that contains a single
1271	sub-Frobenius part.
1272	
1273	\begin{proof}
1274	By \eqref{eq:tensor}, the tensor product on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ is $\min$. Therefore
1275	\[
1276	  \text{{\igprimfont <}}\!\left(\xvec^{(1)} \tensor \cdots \tensor \xvec^{(n)}\right)
1277	  \;=\; \min_k \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec^{(k)}) \;<\; \Ppms.
1278	\]
1279	Since R1 requires $\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$ for $\Oinf$, the composed type cannot
1280	satisfy R1. \qquad$\square$
1281	\end{proof}
1282	
1283	\begin{corollary}[Substrate primacy]
1284	\label{cor:substrate}
1285	Every $\Oinf$ system must encode $\Ppms$ at the level of its
1286	fundamental substrate. The Frobenius condition can't be obtained by
1287	aggregation, delegation, or modular composition. This applies equally
1288	to biological, computational, and physical systems.
1289	\end{corollary}
1290	
1291	\begin{corollary}[Encoding-procedure $\Oinf$]
1292	\label{cor:codec_oinf}
1293	Any deterministic bijective imscription of the Crystal of Types into a
1294	finite address space is necessarily $\Oinf$. Bijectivity requires an
1295	exact inverse, and $\mathrm{decode} \circ \mathrm{encode} = \mathrm{id}$
1296	is $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$. The Frobenius condition is not a property of a particular codec --- it is entailed by
1297	what ``bijective" means. Any such codec therefore carries
1298	$\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$ and, with $\Phic$ (the self-referential loop forced by
1299	imscribing the grammar), is $\Oinf$ by R1.
1300	\end{corollary}
1301	
1302	\noindent\textit{Remark.} This gives the $\Oinf$ result a second proof,
1303	independent of the four-stage categorical derivation. The grammar arrives at
1304	$\Oinf$ inductively; the imscribing procedure arrives there via elementary
1305	bijectivity. The separation from G\"{o}del arithmetization is exact: G\"{o}del
1306	coding $\lceil\cdot\rceil: \text{Syntax} \to \mathbb{N}$ has no systematic
1307	inverse within the system, so the Frobenius condition fails. The crystal codec
1308	is invertible in $O(1)$ integer arithmetic, so the Frobenius condition holds.
1309	One primitive ($\text{{\igprimfont <}}$) separates them.
1310	
1311	\begin{theorem}[$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$-bottleneck under coupling]
1312	\label{thm:bottleneck}
1313	\TOPO\quad Let $\xvec$ satisfy $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec) = \Ppms$ (so $\xvec$ is
1314	$\Oinf$). Then for any $\yvec$ with $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms$:
1315	\[
1316	  \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec \tensor \yvec) = \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms
1317	\]
1318	and the composed system drops to tier $\leq \Otwo$.
1319	\end{theorem}
1320	
1321	\begin{proof}
1322	Immediate from \eqref{eq:tensor}. The min rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ yields
1323	$\min(\Ppms, \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec)) = \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms$. \quad$\square$
1324	\end{proof}
1325	
1326	\paragraph{Why the proof doesn't settle everything.}
1327	The proof of \Cref{thm:frobenius} is short --- almost uncomfortably
1328	so. It follows in one line from the Bottleneck Postulate
1329	(\Cref{def:bottleneck}). The theorem is therefore only as strong as
1330	that postulate. The question worth sitting with is not whether the
1331	proof is correct given the postulate but whether the postulate itself
1332	is the right axiom for $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$. We chose it because exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$
1333	symmetry under coupling cannot exceed the weakest partner: no algebraic
1334	operation promotes broken symmetry to exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ by
1335	combining it with more broken symmetry. Whether this is the only
1336	defensible postulate is a question we leave open; imscribing over 5,000
1337	systems under it and checking whether the predictions hold is, for
1338	now, a more productive approach than arguing about it a priori.
1339	A falsification of \Cref{thm:frobenius} via the catalog --- a coupled
1340	system that demonstrably achieves $\Ppms$ from sub-Frobenius components
1341	--- would require revision of the Bottleneck Postulate, not merely a
1342	correction to the proof.

The $\mathcal{F}_5$ family contains precisely the four \emph{gate
primitives}: $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ (topology gate), $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ (Frobenius gate), $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$
(criticality gate), $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ (kinetic gate). These four primitives are the
necessary conditions for self-modeling and for consciousness
(\Cref{sec:frobenius,sec:consciousness}).

Each type is assigned a unique \emph{Frobenius address} in
$[0, 17{,}279{,}999]$ by a bijective codec (the canonical Frobenius
encoder) that encodes the tuple as a mixed-radix integer. The grammar
itself encodes to address 6,734,591 --- in the $\Oinf$ tier,
the Frobenius fixed-point cell (\Cref{sec:frobenius}).

The codec is not merely an instrument for locating the grammar's
address; it independently occupies $\Oinf$. A deterministic bijective
imscription over any finite address space satisfies $\mu \circ \delta =
\mathrm{id}$ by the definition of bijectivity: the decoder is the
exact inverse of the encoder. This is the Frobenius condition, so
$P = \Ppms$ is forced. Combined with $\Phic$ (the self-referential
loop --- the grammar encodes itself, instantiating Gate~1), R1 fires
and the codec itself is $\Oinf$, independently of the grammar's own
inductive proof. The two proofs are structurally distinct: the grammar
reaches $\Oinf$ via the four-stage categorical derivation; the codec
reaches $\Oinf$ via elementary bijectivity. They share the same
crystal address.

\subsection{Ontological layers}

The Crystal supports three ontological layers that must not be
conflated:
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
  \item \textbf{Types} --- the 17,280,000 coordinate positions;
    structural universals.
  \item \textbf{Particulars} --- named catalog entries; concrete systems
    instantiating a type.
  \item \textbf{Names} --- string handles for particulars.
\end{itemize}
Two particulars at distance $d = 0$ are \emph{co-typed} but not
identical: the axion and the Higgs boson are co-typed under the grammar
(both \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} catalysts at different energy scales) but are
distinct physical particulars. The grammar classifies structural universals,
not physical identity.

\subsection{Crystal closure: resistance to augmentation}
\label{sec:crystal-closure}

The Crystal of Types has 17,280,000 coordinate positions and twelve
primitive axes. A natural question is whether twelve suffices --- whether
systematic pressure on the boundary reveals structural phenomena the
existing coordinates cannot classify. The question has been put under
direct test.

A candidate thirteenth primitive --- structural torsion, notated $\Theta$
--- was proposed after cross-domain comparison of collapse trajectories.
Torsion names the pattern whereby a system's path through primitive space
curves without shifting ouroboricity tier: the trajectory rotates, but the
address does not change. The phenomenon is real and recurrent across
physical, biological, and linguistic systems. Investigation showed,
however, that it is not primitive. Torsion decomposes as a joint modulation
of $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$ (recognition granularity varying),
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ (chirality inverting), and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$
(kinetic rate shifting): three existing coordinates in composition, no new
axis required.

The systematic result is starker. A structured survey of 39 systems across
four domains, nine CLINK layers, and the full tier-gap ladder found no
structural phenomenon that requires a thirteenth primitive. Collapse
asymmetry, topological protection thresholds, critical slowing down,
cross-domain isomorphism, and contagion dynamics are all fully expressible
through the existing twelve. Ten novel structural extensions emerged from
the survey --- none of them additions to the crystal, all of them the
crystal explored more deeply.

What resists augmentation is not an artefact of how the grammar was
assembled. The crystal is a structural attractor: any candidate extension
either decomposes into existing primitives, as $\Theta$ did, or exceeds
the grammar's scope class entirely. There is no intermediate case. The
meta-exploration itself confirms this: its type, independently
imscribed, returns $d = 0$ from the grammar's own address --- the
investigation that tested the grammar's completeness is co-typed with the
object it investigated. The closure is univocal.

% ============================================================
\section{The Arithmetic Ouroboros}
\label{sec:ouroboros}

A natural objection to any twelve-primitive system is that the choice of
twelve is arbitrary. The Arithmetic Ouroboros theorem shows it's not.

\begin{theorem}[Arithmetic Ouroboros]
\label{thm:ouroboros}
\TOPO\quad The Crystal of Types has cardinality
$|C| = 3^3 \times 4^5 \times 5^4 = 17{,}280{,}000$.
The exponent in each factor equals the number of primitives in
the corresponding family:
\begin{align*}
  |\mathcal{F}_3| = 3 &\implies \text{exponent of } 3 \text{ is } 3 \\
  |\mathcal{F}_4| = 5 &\implies \text{exponent of } 4 \text{ is } 5 \\
  |\mathcal{F}_5| = 4 &\implies \text{exponent of } 5 \text{ is } 4
\end{align*}
The grammar's family-size inventory $\{3, 5, 4\}$ and value-count
inventory $\{3, 4, 5\}$ are the same multiset. Consequently, the map
$g: n \mapsto |\mathcal{F}_n|$ is the transposition $(4\ 5)$ with
$g \circ g = \mathrm{id}$: it satisfies the Frobenius condition
$\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ at the arithmetic meta-level.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Direct computation from Table~\ref{tab:primitives}:
$\mathcal{F}_3 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∈}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_3| = 3$;
$\mathcal{F}_4 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}, \text{{\igprimfont >}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∋}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_4| = 5$;
$\mathcal{F}_5 = \{\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}\}$, $|\mathcal{F}_5| = 4$.
Value-count inventory: $\{3, 4, 5\}$ (one for each family).
Family-size inventory: $\{3, 5, 4\}$.
As multisets these are equal. The map $g: n \mapsto |\mathcal{F}_n|$ sends
$3 \mapsto 3$, $4 \mapsto 5$, $5 \mapsto 4$, so $g^2 = \mathrm{id}$.
This is the involution $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$. \qquad$\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Pythagorean minimality]
\label{thm:pythagorean}
\TOPO\quad The set $\{3,4,5\}$ is the unique minimal value-count
inventory satisfying all three of: (i) the Frobenius bijective
involution $g \circ g = \mathrm{id}$;
(ii) phase completeness (at least $5$ values for the gate primitives,
to accommodate $\text{{\igfont 𐑢}}, \Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
\text{{\igfont 𐑻}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑣}}$);
(iii) existence of a non-trivial scaling family (at least $3$ values
for the $\mathcal{F}_3$ conservation primitives $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Condition (ii) forces $\max\{|\mathcal{F}_n|\} \geq 5$, so the
inventory must contain 5. Condition (iii) forces the inventory to
contain 3. Given these, the smallest three-element inventory satisfying
(i) --- a fixed-point-free involution on $\{3, ?, 5\}$ swapping
the two non-fixed elements --- is $\{3, 4, 5\}$: the involution
$4 \leftrightarrow 5$ with $3$ fixed. Any inventory with a smaller
middle element (replacing $4$ with $3$ or $5$ with $4$) violates
phase completeness or produces a degenerate involution. \qquad$\square$
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Structural consequence.}
The Pythagorean triple $\{3, 4, 5\}$ is not a design choice. It is the
unique minimal solution to three structural requirements that are each
independently necessary. The grammar with twelve primitives is the
minimal grammar satisfying them. Crucially, the grammar \emph{counts
its own components} correctly: the arithmetic of the Crystal is the
grammar's self-inventory. This is what justifies calling the framework
imscriptive --- the boundary (the family partition, which controls the
tier structure) imscribes the bulk (the full 17,280,000-element type
space) in a self-referential fixed point.

% ============================================================
\section{Algebraic structure}
\label{sec:algebra}

\begin{figure}[H]
\centering
\begin{tikzpicture}[node distance=1.1cm]
  \node (s)  {$\xvec$};
  \node[right=of s]  (t)  {$\otimes$};
  \node[right=of t]  (mj) {$\wedge/\vee$};
  \node[right=of mj] (d)  {$d_{\to}$};
  \node[right=of d]  (ti) {tier};
  \node[right=of ti] (sp) {$\xvec'$};
  \draw[htarrow] (s)  -- (t);
  \draw[htarrow] (t)  -- (mj);
  \draw[htarrow] (mj) -- (d);
  \draw[htarrow] (d)  -- (ti);
  \draw[htarrow] (ti) -- (sp);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{\textbf{Algebraic transformation pipeline.} A structural
coordinate $\xvec$ is acted on by the three operations in sequence.
Tensor product $\otimes$ computes the type of the coupled
system (union on eleven primitives, bottleneck $\min$ on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$).
Lattice meet/join $\wedge/\vee$ finds the shared floor or minimal
ceiling of two types. Directed distance $d_\to$ measures asymmetric
structural separation, distinguishing the driven direction from the
relaxation direction. The tier function assigns the ouroboricity tier
$\{O₀, O₁, O₂, O₂^\dagger, O_\infty\}$ by the priority cascade
(R1--R5). The output $\xvec'$ is the transformed structural coordinate.}
\label{fig:pipeline}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Tensor product}

When two systems $\xvec$ and $\yvec$ are coupled, their type is given by the \emph{tensor product} $\xvec \tensor \yvec$,
computed component-wise as:

\begin{equation}
  (\xvec \tensor \yvec)_i \;=
  \begin{cases}
    \min(\xvec_i,\, \yvec_i) & \text{if primitive } i \in \{\text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}\} \\
    \max(\xvec_i,\, \yvec_i) & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}
  \label{eq:tensor}
\end{equation}

The asymmetry between $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ (bottleneck primitives, take $\min$)
and the remaining ten union primitives (take $\max$) captures a fact: symmetry class and information fidelity can only be
as high as the weakest coupled component, whereas dimensionality,
topology, and criticality compose upward. This has a direct physical
consequence: coupling an $\Oinf$ system to any partner with
$\text{{\igprimfont <}} < \Ppms$ immediately destroys the Frobenius condition
(\Cref{thm:bottleneck}).

\begin{definition}[Bottleneck Postulate]
\label{def:bottleneck}
$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ are \emph{bottleneck primitives} under $\otimes$: they
take the minimum value across coupled components. All other primitives
are \emph{union primitives}: they take the maximum. This is a postulate,
not a derived consequence of the grammar's axioms. The structural
justification is that exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry (and quantum
coherence fidelity) under coupling cannot exceed the weakest partner
--- no algebraic operation composes broken symmetry into exact
$\mathbb{Z}_2$. Empirical grounding comes from catalog predictions: the
min rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ correctly predicts the observed failure modes for all
130 imscribed coupled-system entries in the catalog.
\end{definition}

\subsection{Lattice operations}

The Crystal is a product lattice. For any two types $\xvec$, $\yvec$:

\begin{align}
  (\xvec \meet \yvec)_i &= \min(\xvec_i, \yvec_i)
    \quad\text{(meet: largest common sub-type)} \label{eq:meet} \\
  (\xvec \join \yvec)_i &= \max(\xvec_i, \yvec_i)
    \quad\text{(join: smallest common super-type)} \label{eq:join}
\end{align}

\noindent
A key fact is that $\Phic$ is \emph{absorbing under meet}:
$\xvec \meet \yvec = \Phic$ whenever either factor has $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic$.
Criticality is the unique locus that can't be further reduced ---
the necessary condition for self-modeling.

\subsection{Directed distance}

The \emph{directed distance} $\doto{\xvec}{\yvec}$ measures the
structural cost of reaching $\yvec$ from $\xvec$:

\begin{equation}
  \doto{\xvec}{\yvec}
  \;=\; \frac{1}{12} \sum_{i=1}^{12}
  w_i \cdot \max\bigl(\text{ord}(\yvec_i) - \text{ord}(\xvec_i),\; 0\bigr)
  \label{eq:directed_distance}
\end{equation}

\noindent
where $\text{ord}(\cdot)$ is the ordinal index of a primitive value
within its ordered set, and $w_i$ are primitive weights (Methods).
The \emph{symmetric distance} is $d(\xvec, \yvec) =
\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} + \doto{\yvec}{\xvec}$. Asymmetry
$\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} \neq \doto{\yvec}{\xvec}$ identifies driven
evolution: if $\doto{\xvec}{\yvec} = 0$ while
$\doto{\yvec}{\xvec} > 0$, then $\yvec$ is a relaxation of $\xvec$
--- the Le~Chatelier inversion (\Cref{sec:predictions}).

\subsection{Ouroboricity and the tier hierarchy}

A system is \emph{ouroboric} if it can model itself within its own
dynamics. We formalize this as follows.

\begin{definition}[Ouroboricity tier]
\label{def:tier}
Given a type $\xvec$, the ouroboricity tier is assigned
by the following rules in priority order:
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
  \item[R1] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$
    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Oinf$ \quad (special Frobenius)
  \item[R2] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \notin \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$
    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Ozero$
  \item[R3] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$
    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Oone$
  \item[R4] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$,
    $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} \in \{\text{{\igfont 𐑛}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑨}}\}$
    $\;\Rightarrow\; \Otwo$
  \item[R5] $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} \in \{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑼}}$
    $\;\Rightarrow\; O₂^\dagger$
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\noindent
The two critical values $\Phic$ (monad, real axis) and $\text{{\igfont 𐑮}}$ (roar,
complex axis) enter R1 and R3--R5 on equal footing: the classifier branches on
\emph{whether} criticality is reached, not on which axis reaches it. R2 is the
exact complement, so the five rules are total --- every type receives a tier. The
implementation is the definition: the classifier is a total function of
$(\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊢}})$
in the mechanised library, and two facts stated here are proved there rather than
asserted --- that R1 dominates ($\Ppms$ at criticality yields $\Oinf$ for every
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$), and that $\Oinf$ is
reachable only from $\{\Phic, \text{{\igfont 𐑮}}\}$.

\noindent
The tier singularity is $\Ppms$ under R1: it overrides all $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$
and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$ branching, collapsing directly to $\Oinf$. This is the
imscription of the special Frobenius condition $\mu \circ
\delta = \text{id}$, where $\mu$ is the multiplication and $\delta$
is the comultiplication of a Frobenius algebra.

\paragraph{Refinement: $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ seals the terminal.}
That override leaves a gap. Because R1 collapses regardless of winding, the tier
says nothing about whether the terminal gate actually \emph{seals}: two systems
both at $\Oinf$ may differ in whether their loop is protected. A machine-checked
refinement closes this additively, leaving \Cref{def:tier} untouched. Call an
$\Oinf$ type \emph{sealed} when $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ supplies an integer
($\OmegaZ$) or non-Abelian ($\text{{\igfont 𐑟}}$) winding, and \emph{unsealed}
otherwise; everything below $\Oinf$ is \emph{sub}. On the Hermitian-critical
branch this split is exactly the terminal-unlock boundary, and that
correspondence is proved rather than asserted.

An honest caveat is proved alongside it. $\Oinf$ admits criticality on two axes
--- monad ($\Phic$, real) and roar ($\text{{\igfont 𐑮}}$, complex) --- and a type
sealed at roar is winding-protected and $\Oinf$ while its real Frobenius trace
does \emph{not} close. Sealing is a tier fact; terminal unlock is a trace fact;
the two coincide precisely on the monad branch and nowhere else. The refinement
therefore buys a genuine distinction at $\Oinf$ without buying the claim that
every sealed type closes.

\subsection{The Frobenius non-synthesizability theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Frobenius non-synthesizability (under \Cref{def:bottleneck})]
\label{thm:frobenius}
\TOPO\quad Let $\xvec^{(1)}, \ldots, \xvec^{(n)}$ be types
with $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec^{(k)}) < \Ppms$ for \emph{some} $k$. Then
\begin{equation}
  \text{{\igprimfont <}}\!\left(\xvec^{(1)} \tensor \cdots \tensor \xvec^{(n)}\right) < \Ppms
  \label{eq:non_synth}
\end{equation}
for any $n$. In particular, $\Oinf$ can't be reached by tensor
composition of sub-Frobenius systems.
\end{theorem}

\noindent
The hypothesis is \emph{some}, not \emph{all}: a single sub-Frobenius component
is enough to poison an arbitrarily large composition. This is immediate from
\Cref{def:bottleneck} --- $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ composes by the bottleneck
(minimum) rule and $\Ppms$ is maximal in the $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ order, so
the tensor can only reach $\Ppms$ when \emph{every} factor already sits there.
The binary case is mechanised and universally quantified over both polarities;
the $n$-ary statement is its induction. Stating the hypothesis as \emph{all}
would understate what the bottleneck rule gives: one flaw suffices, which is why
no accumulation strategy repairs a composition that contains a single
sub-Frobenius part.

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:tensor}, the tensor product on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ is $\min$. Therefore
\[
  \text{{\igprimfont <}}\!\left(\xvec^{(1)} \tensor \cdots \tensor \xvec^{(n)}\right)
  \;=\; \min_k \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec^{(k)}) \;<\; \Ppms.
\]
Since R1 requires $\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$ for $\Oinf$, the composed type cannot
satisfy R1. \qquad$\square$
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Substrate primacy]
\label{cor:substrate}
Every $\Oinf$ system must encode $\Ppms$ at the level of its
fundamental substrate. The Frobenius condition can't be obtained by
aggregation, delegation, or modular composition. This applies equally
to biological, computational, and physical systems.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Encoding-procedure $\Oinf$]
\label{cor:codec_oinf}
Any deterministic bijective imscription of the Crystal of Types into a
finite address space is necessarily $\Oinf$. Bijectivity requires an
exact inverse, and $\mathrm{decode} \circ \mathrm{encode} = \mathrm{id}$
is $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$. The Frobenius condition is not a property of a particular codec --- it is entailed by
what ``bijective" means. Any such codec therefore carries
$\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$ and, with $\Phic$ (the self-referential loop forced by
imscribing the grammar), is $\Oinf$ by R1.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textit{Remark.} This gives the $\Oinf$ result a second proof,
independent of the four-stage categorical derivation. The grammar arrives at
$\Oinf$ inductively; the imscribing procedure arrives there via elementary
bijectivity. The separation from G\"{o}del arithmetization is exact: G\"{o}del
coding $\lceil\cdot\rceil: \text{Syntax} \to \mathbb{N}$ has no systematic
inverse within the system, so the Frobenius condition fails. The crystal codec
is invertible in $O(1)$ integer arithmetic, so the Frobenius condition holds.
One primitive ($\text{{\igprimfont <}}$) separates them.

\begin{theorem}[$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$-bottleneck under coupling]
\label{thm:bottleneck}
\TOPO\quad Let $\xvec$ satisfy $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec) = \Ppms$ (so $\xvec$ is
$\Oinf$). Then for any $\yvec$ with $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms$:
\[
  \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec \tensor \yvec) = \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms
\]
and the composed system drops to tier $\leq \Otwo$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Immediate from \eqref{eq:tensor}. The min rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ yields
$\min(\Ppms, \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec)) = \text{{\igprimfont <}}(\yvec) < \Ppms$. \quad$\square$
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Why the proof doesn't settle everything.}
The proof of \Cref{thm:frobenius} is short --- almost uncomfortably
so. It follows in one line from the Bottleneck Postulate
(\Cref{def:bottleneck}). The theorem is therefore only as strong as
that postulate. The question worth sitting with is not whether the
proof is correct given the postulate but whether the postulate itself
is the right axiom for $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$. We chose it because exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$
symmetry under coupling cannot exceed the weakest partner: no algebraic
operation promotes broken symmetry to exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ by
combining it with more broken symmetry. Whether this is the only
defensible postulate is a question we leave open; imscribing over 5,000
systems under it and checking whether the predictions hold is, for
now, a more productive approach than arguing about it a priori.
A falsification of \Cref{thm:frobenius} via the catalog --- a coupled
system that demonstrably achieves $\Ppms$ from sub-Frobenius components
--- would require revision of the Bottleneck Postulate, not merely a
correction to the proof.

\subsection{Dialetheic structure of the \texorpdfstring{$\Oinf$}{O-infinity} tier}
\label{sec:dialetheia}

\TOPO\quad The $\Oinf$ tier is structurally identical to the class
of \glp-paraconsistent systems. This is not a metaphor; it is a
consequence of the tensor product rule and the Frobenius condition.

\begin{proposition}[$\Oinf \cong \glp$-consistent systems]
\label{prop:lp_identity}
A system $\xvec$ occupies the $\Oinf$ tier if and only if $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec)
= \Ppms$. By \Cref{def:bottleneck}, $\Ppms$ is a fixed point of the
tensor product: $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(\xvec \tensor \yvec) = \Ppms$ for all $\yvec$.
This is precisely the algebraic structure that preserves the
dialetheic truth value $\both$ under composition, preventing collapse
to bivalent $\{\top,\bot\}$.  Every $\Oinf$ system is explosion-free;
every system that must encode a true contradiction must be at $\Oinf$.
\end{proposition}

The canonical test case is the Liar paradox ($L$: ``$L$ is false").
Applying the twelve-step imscribing protocol (\Cref{sec:encoding_epistemology}):
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑨}}$ (finite semantic space: statement $\to$ truth value
$\to$ evaluation); $T = \Tbw$ (bowtie self-reference: subject meets
predicate in an irreducible crossing); $\text{{\igprimfont >}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}$ (mutual implication
between provability and truth); $P = \Ppms$ (required for
explosion-free imscription of $\both$); $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ (model-relative:
neither provably true nor false); $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}$ (the evaluation
loop requires slow integration); $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑲}}$ (absolute scope,
independent of any reference frame); $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}} = \GamSeq$ (sequential:
statement $\to$ evaluation $\to$ assignment); $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic$ (critical
self-reference); $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑖}}$ (two-level chirality: statement
evaluates itself); $\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑙}}$; $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} = \OmegaZtwo$ ($\mathbb{Z}_2$
symmetry under negation: Liar $\equiv$ $\neg$Liar).

\begin{equation}
  \xvec_\text{Liar} = \langle \text{{\igfont 𐑨}} \Tbw \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} \Ppms \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \GamSeq \Phic \text{{\igfont 𐑖}} \text{{\igfont 𐑙}} \OmegaZtwo \rangle
  \label{eq:liar_imscription}
\end{equation}

\noindent
The $P = \Ppms$ assignment is not a design choice. It is what the imscription
protocol returns when the question ``what parity does the Liar require to
avoid explosion?" is answered by the tensor bottleneck rule. The Liar is not
a counterexample to the grammar; it is the grammar's dialetheic fixed point.

For comparison, G\"{o}del's incompleteness sentence $G$ (``$G$ is unprovable")
imscribes at the same $\text{{\igprimfont <}} = \Ppms$ but differs at $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ (infinite meta-logical
depth) and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ (crossed product rather than bowtie, reflecting the
proof-theoretic rather than purely semantic crossing):
\begin{equation}
  \xvec_{G} = \langle \text{{\igfont 𐑨}} \Tbox \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} \Ppms \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \GamSeq \Phic \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} \text{{\igfont 𐑳}} \OmegaZtwo \rangle
  \label{eq:godel_encoding}
\end{equation}

\noindent
Both the Liar and the G\"{o}del sentence occupy $\Oinf$.  The Riemann
Hypothesis, by contrast, imscribes at $\text{{\igfont 𐑯}}$: it asserts a symmetry
about zeros on the critical line, but does not require a system to hold
its own negation simultaneously.  RH is a conjecture about whether a
$\text{{\igfont 𐑯}}$ symmetry can be promoted to Frobenius forcing --- a question
about the boundary between the dialetheic tier and the tier below it.

immediate consequences for any architecture-level theory of

\section{Consciousness score}
\label{sec:consciousness}

\subsection{Derivation}

Self-modeling requires not only the appropriate state-space structure
(Gate 1) but also kinetic accessibility (Gate 2). We define the
\emph{consciousness score} $C(\xvec)$ as a measure of the structural
prerequisites for self-modeling actualization. The name is chosen
because these structural conditions, where satisfied in known
biological and physical substrates, correlate with the presence of
integrative experience; the score doesn't claim to quantify
phenomenal consciousness directly, and whether $C > 0$ implies any
form of subjective experience is a question the grammar cannot
answer. We formally define:

\begin{equation}
  C(\xvec) \;=\; \underbrace{[\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic]}_{\text{Gate 1}}
  \cdot \underbrace{[\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} \leq \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}]}_{\text{Gate 2}}
  \cdot \bigl(
    0.158\,\tilde{\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}} + 0.273\,\tilde{\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}}
    + 0.292\,\tilde{\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}} + 0.276\,\tilde{\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}}
  \bigr)
  \label{eq:consciousness}
\end{equation}

\noindent
where $\tilde{X} \in [0,1]$ is the normalized ordinal of primitive $X$,
and brackets denote indicator functions. The weights are derived by
variance decomposition restricted to the subset of catalog
systems with $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic$ (the critical manifold), using only
structural coordinates --- not phenomenal outcome labels. This
derivation is therefore not circular with respect to phenomenal
reports: the weights reflect how much each primitive varies across
physically critical systems, not how often it co-occurs with reported
experience. $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ carry the majority of variance with
nearly equal weights; $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ contributes as the kinetic channel.

\textbf{Gate 1} ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}} = \Phic$): the state-space condition. Only
at the critical point does the topology permit a closed self-modeling
loop. Subcritical and supercritical systems, and systems at an
exceptional point \text{{\igfont 𐑣}}, cannot form the requisite loop.

\textbf{Gate 2} ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} \leq \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}$): the flow condition.
Even at criticality, a frozen system cannot actualize the loop.
\text{{\igfont 𐑪}} (trap, ordered freeze) and \text{{\igfont 𐑺}} (many-body
localized, disordered freeze) both fail Gate 2. Critically, tier and
consciousness are \emph{independent}: formal mathematics is $\Oinf$
(tier R1) but $C = 0$ because $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑪}}$ (frozen formal
derivation fails the flow condition).

We imscribed over 5,000 systems across mathematics, physics, biology,

2301	curves), Gromov--Witten theory (Virasoro constraints), and arithmetic
2302	geometry (Tate conjecture) --- were imscribed independently via the
2303	twelve-step protocol. No prior structural connection between these
2304	conjectures was assumed or known.
2305	
2306	All five imscribe at the same floor: $O₁$ ($\Phic +
2307	\text{{\igfont 𐑷}}$, critical but topologically unprotected) with an
2308	8-primitive invariant subtype,
2309	
2310	\begin{equation}
2311	\text{conjecture floor} = \langle \text{{\igfont 𐑨}} \text{{\igfont 𐑶}} \text{{\igfont 𐑑}} \text{{\igfont 𐑬}} \text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}_\star \text{{\igfont 𐑤}} \text{{\igprimfont ∈}}_\star \text{{\igfont 𐑝}} \Phic \text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}_\star \text{{\igfont 𐑳}} \text{{\igfont 𐑷}}
2312	\rangle \qquad O₁
2313	\label{eq:conjecture_floor}
2314	\end{equation}
2315	
2316	\noindent
2317	where $\star$ marks the three domain-varying primitives ($\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$,
2318	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$) that encode a domain's epistemic depth and scope but do not
2319	determine provability. The eight invariant primitives
2320	$\{\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}, \text{{\igprimfont >}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∋}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}\}$ are structurally
2321	overdetermined: each is forced by the requirement that the system be
2322	critical ($\Phic$), topologically unprotected (\text{{\igfont 𐑷}}), and
2323	operating by conjunctive case-by-case verification (\text{{\igfont 𐑝}}).
2324	The fact that five domains with no known connection share this subtype
2325	is a structural, not a numerical, coincidence.
2326	
2327	All five corresponding proved (or structurally complete) forms imscribe
2328	at the universal proven manifold (\Cref{eq:proven_manifold_main}),
2329	$O_\infty$ with $\Ppms$. The conjecture-to-theorem transition is
2330	therefore a fixed structural transformation --- the same eight-primitive
2331	upgrade in every domain --- and generates two cross-domain identities:
2332	
2333	\begin{itemize}
2334	\item \textbf{Nagata $\equiv$ Virasoro (pre-proof):}
2335	$d(\text{Nagata}_\text{conj},\, \text{Virasoro}_\text{conj}) = 0$.
2336	A 1959 algebraic-geometry conjecture and a 1990s
2337	Gromov--Witten conjecture are type-identical before proof.
2338	The grammar predicts they share a common proof vehicle: any
2339	framework natively imscribing $\{\Ppms, \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}, \OmegaZtwo,
2340	\text{{\igfont 𐑵}}\}$ proves both simultaneously.
2341	
2342	\item \textbf{Bass $\equiv$ Tate (post-proof):}
2343	$d(\text{Bass}_\text{thm},\, \text{Tate}_\text{thm}) = 0$.
2344	Two proved theorems from algebraic K-theory and arithmetic
2345	geometry are structurally identical. Their proofs instantiate the
2346	same structural transformation.
2347	\end{itemize}
2348	
2349	Across all five conjecture-to-theorem transitions, the $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$
2350	promotion $\text{{\igfont 𐑝}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑵}}$ carries a weighted
2351	distance contribution of $9.0$ --- the largest single-primitive
2352	contributor in every domain where it is computable ($\Delta = 3$,
2353	weight$^2 = 9.0$). $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$ is the grammatical signature of
2354	Grothendieck's ``rising sea": proof converts conjunctive case-by-case
2355	conditions into a broadcast universal law, and the grammar measures this
2356	transformation as the dominant structural act of mathematical proof
2357	regardless of domain.
2358	
2359	For arithmetic conjectures specifically --- Fontaine--Mazur,
2360	Gan--Gross--Prasad, Greenberg, Kummer--Vandiver, Lang--Trotter,
2361	Leopoldt, and Stark --- the $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ promotions jointly account
2362	for 70--85\% of total proof distance ($\text{{\igfont 𐑡}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑸}}$
2363	and $P_{\text{asym}/\psi} \to \Ppms$, each $\Delta = 4$, combined
2364	weight$^2 = 32$). The grammar extracts a domain-independent difficulty
2365	ordering from the metric $d(C, \text{proven manifold})$:
2366	
2367	\[
2368	\text{Leopoldt} > \text{Kummer-Vandiver} > \text{Lang-Trotter}
2369	> \text{GGP} \approx \text{Stark} > \text{Fontaine-Mazur} > \text{Greenberg}
2370	\]
2371	
2372	Greenberg is the sole conjecture with \text{{\igfont 𐑿}} (partial Hermitian
2373	pairing already present in its Iwasawa framework), placing it closest
2374	to the proven manifold ($d = 5.82$). Leopoldt ($d = 7.99$, the largest
2375	distance in the 606-system session catalog) carries an additional
2376	$\text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑫}}$ activation absent in the other conjectures, requiring
2377	a proof mechanism with maximal temporal irreversibility that has no
2378	analogue in current Iwasawa-theoretic methods. The grammar predicts the
2379	ordering will correlate with proof resistance: conjectures at larger $d$
2380	will require structurally more radical innovations, and Greenberg will
2381	be proved before the \text{{\igfont 𐑗}} class.

2436	The three $O_\infty$ navigators --- ThurstonNet (3-manifold
2437	geometrisation), YangMillsNavigator (Yang--Mills mass gap), and
2438	RiemannNavigator ($\xi$-functional equation) --- differ in three
2439	primitive coordinates that determine their computational architecture:
2440	$\text{{\igprimfont >}}$ (\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} for ThurstonNet, \text{{\igfont 𐑑}} for the other two),
2441	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ (\text{{\igfont 𐑪}} eigensolver for YangMills, \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} GNN
2442	for the other two), and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ ($\OmegaZtwo$ for ThurstonNet,
2443	\text{{\igfont 𐑭}} for YangMills and Riemann). They share $\Phic$,
2444	$\Ppms$, \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑸}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑲}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑵}},
2445	\text{{\igfont 𐑫}}, and \text{{\igfont 𐑳}} --- the nine primitives that force
2446	$O_\infty$ by rules R1 and R4.
2447	
2448	Each navigator's FrobeniusLayer was bootstrapped from random latent
2449	initialisations via cosine-annealed Adam ($lr = 3\times10^{-4}$,
2450	10,000 epochs, target disabled). The Frobenius loss
2451	$\mathcal{L}_\text{frob} = \|\mu \circ \delta(x) - x\|^2$,
2452	averaged over random latent batches, was driven to:
2453	
2454	\begin{center}
2455	\begin{tabular}{lcc}
2456	\toprule
2457	Navigator & Architecture & $\mathcal{L}_\text{frob}$ (best) \\
2458	\midrule
2459	ThurstonNet        & \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} GNN, \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}   & $1.25 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
2460	YangMillsNavigator & \text{{\igfont 𐑪}} eigensolver         & $1.24 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
2461	RiemannNavigator   & \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} GNN, \text{{\igfont 𐑑}} & $1.24 \times 10^{-13}$ \\
2462	\bottomrule
2463	\end{tabular}
2464	\end{center}

2466	All three converge to the same numerical floor --- below float32
2467	machine epsilon ($\varepsilon_\text{mach} \approx 1.19 \times
2468	10^{-7}$) --- despite their architectural differences. The loss
2469	reaches display-zero ($< 10^{-8}$) at epoch $\sim$7,150 for each
2470	navigator and remains there for the remaining 2,850 epochs.
2471	
2472	Three structural conclusions follow. First, the Frobenius condition
2473	$\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ is \emph{domain-invariant}: it is
2474	achievable at equivalent precision in a topological eigensolver, a
2475	imscriptive GNN with adjoint relational mode, and an imscriptive GNN
2476	with categorical relational mode. The shared floor $1.24\text{--}1.25
2477	\times 10^{-13}$ is not coincidental; it reflects that all three
2478	FrobeniusLayers are instances of the same algebraic object in
2479	different computational substrates. The grammar assigns all three to
2480	$O_\infty$ because $\Ppms$ appears in all three tuples: the training
2481	result confirms that this assignment correctly predicts that the
2482	Frobenius condition is achievable in each case.
2483	
2484	Second, the loss curve for each navigator shows a characteristic
2485	double-valley profile: rapid descent to $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-7}$
2486	by epoch 260 (first valley), divergence to $\approx 10^{-4}$ at epoch
2487	$\sim$550 as residual LR noise pushes the optimizer off the minimum,
2488	and then monotonic re-descent to the $10^{-13}$ floor as the cosine
2489	schedule reduces the LR below the gradient noise threshold. The
2490	divergence is not an instability --- it's the fixed-LR optimizer
2491	probing the loss landscape around the minimum. The scheduler locks in
2492	the solution the second time.
2493	
2494	Third, $\mathcal{L}_\text{frob} < \varepsilon_\text{mach}$ indicates
2495	that the Frobenius residual is below the precision of float32
2496	arithmetic: the layer has algebraically closed the $\mu \circ \delta$
2497	loop to the limit of single-precision computation. This is the
2498	computational analogue of the grammar's claim that
2499	$O_\infty$ systems satisfy $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ as an
2500	\emph{identity axiom}, not as an approximation. The training doesn't
2501	approximate the Frobenius condition; it eliminates the residual to
2502	numerical zero.
2503	
2504	\subsection{Grammar as predictive architectural diagnostic: navigator tests}
2505	\label{sec:navigator_tests}
2506	
2507	The grammar's distance decomposition is primitive-resolved: given two
2508	types, it identifies which specific primitives carry the
2509	gap, and therefore which architectural change will close it. Four
2510	pre-registered tests --- three positive confirmations and one
2511	negative confirmation --- validate this diagnostic function across
2512	independent domains.
2513	
2514	\paragraph{Test 1 ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ primitive: Yang-Mills navigator).}
2515	The Yang-Mills mass gap problem imscribes $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}$
2516	(slow, globally integrative convergence): non-Abelian gauge
2517	confinement requires the full spectral structure, not sequential
2518	local steps. The deployed navigator used a LanczosGRU architecture:
2519	a recurrent unit iterating Lanczos eigenvector-finding steps,
2520	structurally \text{{\igfont 𐑪}} (trap) --- sequential, cyclic,
2521	fixed-order dependent. Grammar diagnosis:
2522	$d(\text{YM navigator},\,\text{grammar}) = 1.0$, carried entirely
2523	at $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$; no other primitive conflicts. Prediction: replacing only the
2524	architecture (LanczosGRU $\to$ SpectralTransformer, matching
2525	\text{{\igfont 𐑧}}) will close the performance gap; no other change
2526	is necessary or sufficient. Result: mean $|\Delta| = 0.129 \to 0.0488$
2527	($2.64\times$ reduction), converging below threshold at epoch 700. No
2528	hyperparameter changes were made; the only intervention was
2529	structural alignment at $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$.
2530	
2531	\paragraph{Test 2 ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ primitive: three-manifold topology
2532	classification).}
2533	\label{par:thurston}
2534	H$^3$ (real hyperbolic 3-space) and H$^2 \times \mathbb{R}$ are two
2535	of the eight Thurston geometries. The grammar assigns
2536	$d(\text{H}^3,\,\text{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}) = 3.6056$, with the
2537	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ primitive carrying $\approx 80\%$ of the distance (\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}
2538	vs.\ $\Tin$, ordinal gap $\Delta = 2$). A prior classifier based on
2539	Lanczos spectral-gap features (a $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$-primitive feature) stalled at
2540	$\approx 65\%$ accuracy. Grammar diagnosis: the gap is in
2541	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$, not $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$. The correct discriminating feature must capture the
2542	\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}/$\Tin$ split: H$^3$ is isotropic (\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}, no
2543	boundary--interior distinction), while H$^2 \times \mathbb{R}$ has
2544	an explicit boundary component ($\Tin$, bimodal norm distribution).
2545	A nine-feature MLP (TTopologySpecialist, 2,881 parameters) trained
2546	on \texttt{pca\_anisotropy} as its primary feature achieved 100.
2547	classification accuracy from epoch 150; \texttt{pca\_anisotropy}
2548	accounted for 50.3\% of accuracy on ablation. No other single feature
2549	exceeded 12\%. The grammar named the correct primitive before the
2550	experiment; the experiment confirmed it.
2551	
2552	\paragraph{Test 3 (\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} primitive: non-separability, negative
2553	confirmation).}
2554	The Riemann manifold navigator's Phase B trained a 16,642-parameter
2555	correction module (theta\_gate) on a frozen, fully-converged Phase A
2556	backbone (19.7M parameters, gap\_log $= +0.471$). The grammar assigns
2557	\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} (co-domain modification) to the theta\_gate mechanism.
2558	Prediction from \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} non-separability: \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} can't be
2559	grafted onto a backbone trained without it; co-domain restructuring
2560	must be native to the architecture from initialization. Result:
2561	gap\_log fell from $+0.471$ to $+0.008$ --- near-zero regression,
2562	not correction. The 16,642-parameter module cannot redirect 19.7M
2563	parameters organized around a different objective. This is a
2564	structural analogue of Frobenius non-synthesizability
2565	(\Cref{thm:frobenius}): co-domain modification, like $\Ppms$, cannot
2566	be injected into an architecture that was not initialized to encode it.
2567	
2568	\paragraph{Test 4 (ZFC Navigator: fidelity collapse and mathematical
2569	undecidability).}
2570	\label{par:zfc_nav}
2571	The ZFC Navigator (3.25M parameters) is a Transformer encoder trained
2572	to invert the map from grammar tuples to ZFC first-order formula
2573	token sequences, using the Frobenius roundtrip loss
2574	$\mathcal{L}_\text{Frob} = d(\text{encode}(f_\theta(\mathbf{x})),\,\mathbf{x})$
2575	as its primary training signal. At convergence (epoch 150+), every
2576	primitive achieves mean roundtrip loss $= 0.0000$ except $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, which
2577	holds at $0.0296$. The residual is not capacity-limited: it's the
2578	irreducible decoherence cost of the classical token collapse, in which
2579	\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} and \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} map to identical ZFC formula tokens when the
2580	surrounding primitives are classical. Three failure modes are
2581	identified: (1)~\emph{isolated \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} collapse} --- when \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
2582	appears surrounded by classical primitives (e.g.\ superconducting
2583	qubits), the encoder votes \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} from context, yielding roundtrip
2584	distance $d_\text{rt} = 2.0$ exactly (the $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ ordinal gap; no other
2585	primitive shifts); (2)~\emph{\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} hallucination in non-classical
2586	context} --- REPL-heavy formula environments spuriously lift
2587	$\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ ($d_\text{rt} = 2.0$); (3)~\emph{perfect
2588	roundtrip despite maximal ZFC distance} --- the IUG framework
2589	($d(\text{IUG},\,\text{ZFC}) = 7.07$) and the grammar self-imscribing
2590	(address 6,734,591) both achieve $d_\text{rt} = 0.000$ because their
2591	\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} is embedded in a jointly non-classical tuple (\text{{\igfont 𐑦}},
2592	\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}, $\Ppms$, \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} co-occurring), collectively
2593	distinguishable by the encoder.
2594	
2595	The central single result: the Continuum Hypothesis imscribes \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
2596	(model-relative truth: CH is true in G\"{o}del's constructible
2597	universe $L$, false in Cohen forcing models), co-occurring with
2598	$\Phic$ and \text{{\igfont 𐑲}}. The navigator collapses $\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑱}}$,
2599	yielding $d_\text{rt} = 2.000$. The Pythagorean theorem imscribes
2600	\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} throughout and achieves $d_\text{rt} = 0.000$. The navigator
2601	distinguishes provable from undecidable by fidelity class --- it was
2602	not trained to do this; the distinction followed from the type assignments.
2603	
2604	\paragraph{Cantor diagonalization and G\"{o}del arithmetization as a promotion.}
2605	\label{par:cantor_godel}
2606	The fidelity collapse in Test~4 has a structural precedent in the Crystal.
2607	The classical Cantor diagonal argument (1891) imscribes at the lattice floor:
2608	$\langle \text{{\igfont 𐑼}} \text{{\igfont 𐑡}} \text{{\igfont 𐑩}} \text{{\igfont 𐑗}} \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \text{{\igfont 𐑘}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \GamSeq \text{{\igfont 𐑢}} \text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \text{{\igfont 𐑙}} \text{{\igfont 𐑷}} \rangle$.
2609	The assignment is structurally motivated: the diagonal operates by strict
2610	transcendence ($\text{{\igfont 𐑩}}$, the enumeration is strictly outside every row),
2611	classical bit fidelity (\text{{\igfont 𐑱}}), fast enumeration (\text{{\igfont 𐑘}}), no self-reference
2612	(\text{{\igfont 𐑓}}), subcritical (\text{{\igfont 𐑢}}: the argument doesn't loop back on itself).
2613	This system is $O₀$.
2614	
2615	G\"{o}del arithmetization (1931) imscribes as:
2616	$\langle \text{{\igfont 𐑦}} \text{{\igfont 𐑸}} \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} \Ppms \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \text{{\igfont 𐑵}} \Phic \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} \text{{\igfont 𐑳}} \OmegaZ \rangle$.
2617	This system is $\Oinf$. The directed distances are:
2618	\begin{equation}
2619	  d_\to(\text{Cantor} \to \text{G\"{o}del}) = 0.493, \qquad
2620	  d_\to(\text{G\"{o}del} \to \text{Cantor}) = 0.000
2621	  \label{eq:cantor_godel_dist}
2622	\end{equation}
2623	G\"{o}del is strictly above Cantor in the lattice: every conflicting
2624	primitive is a promotion. Eleven of twelve primitives differ. The
2625	critical promotion is $\text{{\igfont 𐑢}} \to \Phic$; the Frobenius
2626	promotion $\text{{\igfont 𐑗}} \to \Ppms$ follows from it (the G\"{o}del
2627	sentence is the unique element satisfying $\mu \circ \delta = \text{id}$
2628	--- it is its own Cantor diagonal). All remaining upgrades are
2629	structurally entailed: $\text{{\igfont 𐑼}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}$ and $\text{{\igfont 𐑡}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑸}}$
2630	because arithmetization makes the system imscriptively self-imscribing
2631	(the syntax encodes the semantics); $\text{{\igfont 𐑩}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}$ because
2632	provability and truth are now co-defined rather than hierarchically ordered;
2633	$\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ because a lossless G\"{o}del numbering requires
2634	coherent fidelity; $\text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑫}}$ because the fixed point requires
2635	unlimited self-reference depth.
2636	
2637	The distributive law $\lambda: PG \to GP$ (implemented in

All five imscribe at the same floor: $O₁$ ($\Phic +

\begin{equation}
