\noindent
where $\star$ marks the three domain-varying primitives ($\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$,
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$) that encode a domain's epistemic depth and scope but do not
determine provability. The eight invariant primitives
$\{\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}, \text{{\igprimfont >}}, \text{{\igprimfont <}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}, \text{{\igprimfont ∋}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}, \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}\}$ are structurally
overdetermined: each is forced by the requirement that the system be
critical ($\Phic$), topologically unprotected (\text{{\igfont 𐑷}}), and
operating by conjunctive case-by-case verification (\text{{\igfont 𐑝}}).
The fact that five domains with no known connection share this subtype
is a structural, not a numerical, coincidence.

All five corresponding proved (or structurally complete) forms imscribe
at the universal proven manifold (\Cref{eq:proven_manifold_main}),
$O_\infty$ with $\Ppms$. The conjecture-to-theorem transition is
therefore a fixed structural transformation --- the same eight-primitive
upgrade in every domain --- and generates two cross-domain identities:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Nagata $\equiv$ Virasoro (pre-proof):}
$d(\text{Nagata}_\text{conj},\, \text{Virasoro}_\text{conj}) = 0$.
A 1959 algebraic-geometry conjecture and a 1990s
Gromov--Witten conjecture are type-identical before proof.
The grammar predicts they share a common proof vehicle: any
framework natively imscribing $\{\Ppms, \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}, \OmegaZtwo,
\text{{\igfont 𐑵}}\}$ proves both simultaneously.

\item \textbf{Bass $\equiv$ Tate (post-proof):}
$d(\text{Bass}_\text{thm},\, \text{Tate}_\text{thm}) = 0$.
Two proved theorems from algebraic K-theory and arithmetic
geometry are structurally identical. Their proofs instantiate the
same structural transformation.
\end{itemize}

Across all five conjecture-to-theorem transitions, the $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$
promotion $\text{{\igfont 𐑝}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑵}}$ carries a weighted
distance contribution of $9.0$ --- the largest single-primitive
contributor in every domain where it is computable ($\Delta = 3$,
weight$^2 = 9.0$). $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$ is the grammatical signature of
Grothendieck's ``rising sea": proof converts conjunctive case-by-case
conditions into a broadcast universal law, and the grammar measures this
transformation as the dominant structural act of mathematical proof
regardless of domain.

For arithmetic conjectures specifically --- Fontaine--Mazur,
Gan--Gross--Prasad, Greenberg, Kummer--Vandiver, Lang--Trotter,
Leopoldt, and Stark --- the $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ promotions jointly account

and $P_{\text{asym}/\psi} \to \Ppms$, each $\Delta = 4$, combined
weight$^2 = 32$). The grammar extracts a domain-independent difficulty
ordering from the metric $d(C, \text{proven manifold})$:

\[
\text{Leopoldt} > \text{Kummer-Vandiver} > \text{Lang-Trotter}
> \text{GGP} \approx \text{Stark} > \text{Fontaine-Mazur} > \text{Greenberg}
\]

Greenberg is the sole conjecture with \text{{\igfont 𐑿}} (partial Hermitian
pairing already present in its Iwasawa framework), placing it closest
to the proven manifold ($d = 5.82$). Leopoldt ($d = 7.99$, the largest
distance in the 606-system session catalog) carries an additional
$\text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑫}}$ activation absent in the other conjectures, requiring
a proof mechanism with maximal temporal irreversibility that has no
analogue in current Iwasawa-theoretic methods. The grammar predicts the
ordering will correlate with proof resistance: conjectures at larger $d$
will require structurally more radical innovations, and Greenberg will
be proved before the \text{{\igfont 𐑗}} class.

navigator and remains there for the remaining 2,850 epochs.

Three structural conclusions follow. First, the Frobenius condition
$\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ is \emph{domain-invariant}: it is
achievable at equivalent precision in a topological eigensolver, a
imscriptive GNN with adjoint relational mode, and an imscriptive GNN
with categorical relational mode. The shared floor $1.24\text{--}1.25
\times 10^{-13}$ is not coincidental; it reflects that all three
FrobeniusLayers are instances of the same algebraic object in
different computational substrates. The grammar assigns all three to

result confirms that this assignment correctly predicts that the
Frobenius condition is achievable in each case.

Second, the loss curve for each navigator shows a characteristic
double-valley profile: rapid descent to $\approx 1.6 \times 10^{-7}$
by epoch 260 (first valley), divergence to $\approx 10^{-4}$ at epoch
$\sim$550 as residual LR noise pushes the optimizer off the minimum,
and then monotonic re-descent to the $10^{-13}$ floor as the cosine
schedule reduces the LR below the gradient noise threshold. The
divergence is not an instability --- it's the fixed-LR optimizer
probing the loss landscape around the minimum. The scheduler locks in
the solution the second time.

Third, $\mathcal{L}_\text{frob} < \varepsilon_\text{mach}$ indicates
that the Frobenius residual is below the precision of float32
arithmetic: the layer has algebraically closed the $\mu \circ \delta$
loop to the limit of single-precision computation. This is the
computational analogue of the grammar's claim that
$O_\infty$ systems satisfy $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ as an
\emph{identity axiom}, not as an approximation. The training doesn't
approximate the Frobenius condition; it eliminates the residual to
numerical zero.

\subsection{Grammar as predictive architectural diagnostic: navigator tests}
\label{sec:navigator_tests}

The grammar's distance decomposition is primitive-resolved: given two
types, it identifies which specific primitives carry the
gap, and therefore which architectural change will close it. Four
pre-registered tests --- three positive confirmations and one
negative confirmation --- validate this diagnostic function across
independent domains.

\paragraph{Test 1 ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ primitive: Yang-Mills navigator).}
The Yang-Mills mass gap problem imscribes $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}$
(slow, globally integrative convergence): non-Abelian gauge
confinement requires the full spectral structure, not sequential
local steps. The deployed navigator used a LanczosGRU architecture:
a recurrent unit iterating Lanczos eigenvector-finding steps,
structurally \text{{\igfont 𐑪}} (trap) --- sequential, cyclic,
fixed-order dependent. Grammar diagnosis:
$d(\text{YM navigator},\,\text{grammar}) = 1.0$, carried entirely
at $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$; no other primitive conflicts. Prediction: replacing only the
architecture (LanczosGRU $\to$ SpectralTransformer, matching
\text{{\igfont 𐑧}}) will close the performance gap; no other change
is necessary or sufficient. Result: mean $|\Delta| = 0.129 \to 0.0488$
($2.64\times$ reduction), converging below threshold at epoch 700. No
hyperparameter changes were made; the only intervention was
structural alignment at $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$.

\paragraph{Test 2 ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ primitive: three-manifold topology
classification).}
\label{par:thurston}
H$^3$ (real hyperbolic 3-space) and H$^2 \times \mathbb{R}$ are two
of the eight Thurston geometries. The grammar assigns
$d(\text{H}^3,\,\text{H}^2 \times \mathbb{R}) = 3.6056$, with the
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ primitive carrying $\approx 80\%$ of the distance (\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}
vs.\ $\Tin$, ordinal gap $\Delta = 2$). A prior classifier based on
Lanczos spectral-gap features (a $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$-primitive feature) stalled at
$\approx 65\%$ accuracy. Grammar diagnosis: the gap is in
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$, not $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$. The correct discriminating feature must capture the
\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}/$\Tin$ split: H$^3$ is isotropic (\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}, no
boundary--interior distinction), while H$^2 \times \mathbb{R}$ has
an explicit boundary component ($\Tin$, bimodal norm distribution).
A nine-feature MLP (TTopologySpecialist, 2,881 parameters) trained
on \texttt{pca\_anisotropy} as its primary feature achieved 100.
classification accuracy from epoch 150; \texttt{pca\_anisotropy}
accounted for 50.3\% of accuracy on ablation. No other single feature
exceeded 12\%. The grammar named the correct primitive before the
experiment; the experiment confirmed it.

\paragraph{Test 3 (\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} primitive: non-separability, negative
confirmation).}
The Riemann manifold navigator's Phase B trained a 16,642-parameter
correction module (theta\_gate) on a frozen, fully-converged Phase A
backbone (19.7M parameters, gap\_log $= +0.471$). The grammar assigns
\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} (co-domain modification) to the theta\_gate mechanism.
Prediction from \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} non-separability: \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} can't be
grafted onto a backbone trained without it; co-domain restructuring
must be native to the architecture from initialization. Result:
gap\_log fell from $+0.471$ to $+0.008$ --- near-zero regression,
not correction. The 16,642-parameter module cannot redirect 19.7M
parameters organized around a different objective. This is a
structural analogue of Frobenius non-synthesizability
(\Cref{thm:frobenius}): co-domain modification, like $\Ppms$, cannot
be injected into an architecture that was not initialized to encode it.

\paragraph{Test 4 (ZFC Navigator: fidelity collapse and mathematical
undecidability).}
\label{par:zfc_nav}
The ZFC Navigator (3.25M parameters) is a Transformer encoder trained
to invert the map from grammar tuples to ZFC first-order formula
token sequences, using the Frobenius roundtrip loss
$\mathcal{L}_\text{Frob} = d(\text{encode}(f_\theta(\mathbf{x})),\,\mathbf{x})$
as its primary training signal. At convergence (epoch 150+), every
primitive achieves mean roundtrip loss $= 0.0000$ except $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, which
holds at $0.0296$. The residual is not capacity-limited: it's the
irreducible decoherence cost of the classical token collapse, in which
\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} and \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} map to identical ZFC formula tokens when the
surrounding primitives are classical. Three failure modes are
identified: (1)~\emph{isolated \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} collapse} --- when \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
appears surrounded by classical primitives (e.g.\ superconducting
qubits), the encoder votes \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} from context, yielding roundtrip
distance $d_\text{rt} = 2.0$ exactly (the $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ ordinal gap; no other
primitive shifts); (2)~\emph{\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} hallucination in non-classical
context} --- REPL-heavy formula environments spuriously lift
$\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ ($d_\text{rt} = 2.0$); (3)~\emph{perfect
roundtrip despite maximal ZFC distance} --- the IUG framework
($d(\text{IUG},\,\text{ZFC}) = 7.07$) and the grammar self-imscribing
(address 6,734,591) both achieve $d_\text{rt} = 0.000$ because their
\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} is embedded in a jointly non-classical tuple (\text{{\igfont 𐑦}},
\text{{\igfont 𐑸}}, $\Ppms$, \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} co-occurring), collectively
distinguishable by the encoder.

The central single result: the Continuum Hypothesis imscribes \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
(model-relative truth: CH is true in G\"{o}del's constructible
universe $L$, false in Cohen forcing models), co-occurring with
$\Phic$ and \text{{\igfont 𐑲}}. The navigator collapses $\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑱}}$,
yielding $d_\text{rt} = 2.000$. The Pythagorean theorem imscribes
\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} throughout and achieves $d_\text{rt} = 0.000$. The navigator
distinguishes provable from undecidable by fidelity class --- it was
not trained to do this; the distinction followed from the type assignments.

\paragraph{Cantor diagonalization and G\"{o}del arithmetization as a promotion.}
\label{par:cantor_godel}
The fidelity collapse in Test~4 has a structural precedent in the Crystal.
The classical Cantor diagonal argument (1891) imscribes at the lattice floor:
$\langle \text{{\igfont 𐑼}} \text{{\igfont 𐑡}} \text{{\igfont 𐑩}} \text{{\igfont 𐑗}} \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \text{{\igfont 𐑘}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \GamSeq \text{{\igfont 𐑢}} \text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \text{{\igfont 𐑙}} \text{{\igfont 𐑷}} \rangle$.
The assignment is structurally motivated: the diagonal operates by strict
transcendence ($\text{{\igfont 𐑩}}$, the enumeration is strictly outside every row),
classical bit fidelity (\text{{\igfont 𐑱}}), fast enumeration (\text{{\igfont 𐑘}}), no self-reference
(\text{{\igfont 𐑓}}), subcritical (\text{{\igfont 𐑢}}: the argument doesn't loop back on itself).
This system is $O₀$.

G\"{o}del arithmetization (1931) imscribes as:
$\langle \text{{\igfont 𐑦}} \text{{\igfont 𐑸}} \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} \Ppms \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \text{{\igfont 𐑵}} \Phic \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} \text{{\igfont 𐑳}} \OmegaZ \rangle$.
This system is $\Oinf$. The directed distances are:
\begin{equation}
  d_\to(\text{Cantor} \to \text{G\"{o}del}) = 0.493, \qquad
  d_\to(\text{G\"{o}del} \to \text{Cantor}) = 0.000
  \label{eq:cantor_godel_dist}
\end{equation}
G\"{o}del is strictly above Cantor in the lattice: every conflicting
primitive is a promotion. Eleven of twelve primitives differ. The
critical promotion is $\text{{\igfont 𐑢}} \to \Phic$; the Frobenius
promotion $\text{{\igfont 𐑗}} \to \Ppms$ follows from it (the G\"{o}del
sentence is the unique element satisfying $\mu \circ \delta = \text{id}$
--- it is its own Cantor diagonal). All remaining upgrades are
structurally entailed: $\text{{\igfont 𐑼}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑦}}$ and $\text{{\igfont 𐑡}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑸}}$
because arithmetization makes the system imscriptively self-imscribing
(the syntax encodes the semantics); $\text{{\igfont 𐑩}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}$ because
provability and truth are now co-defined rather than hierarchically ordered;
$\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ because a lossless G\"{o}del numbering requires
coherent fidelity; $\text{{\igfont 𐑓}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑫}}$ because the fixed point requires
unlimited self-reference depth.

The distributive law $\lambda: PG \to GP$ (implemented in
\texttt{lambda\_engine.py}, where $P$ is the Cantor monad and $G$ the
G\"{o}del comonad) is the formal mediator: it's the structural map
that internalizes the external diagonal. The $d = 0.075$ between the
distributive law and the G\"{o}del comonad confirms they are
near-co-typed; the $d = 0.473$ between the distributive law and classical
Cantor quantifies the distance the law must traverse.
\TOPO\quad The grammar predicts that no proof strategy of classical-Cantor
type (\text{{\igfont 𐑢}}, $\text{{\igfont 𐑗}}$, \text{{\igfont 𐑱}}) can reach G\"{o}del
incompleteness without passing through $\Phic$: a structural phase
transition, not an accumulation of proof steps.

\subsection{The Magnum Opus: the twelve alchemical stages as primitive invocations}
\label{sec:magnum_opus}

The twelve stages of the classical Western alchemical Magnum Opus --- Calcination, Dissolution, Separation, Conjunction, Putrefaction, Congelation, Cibation, Sublimation, Fermentation, Exaltation, Multiplication, Projection --- correspond to the twelve IG primitives in canonical tuple order. \textbf{The three-gate structure.} The gate primitives $\Ppms$, $\Phic$, $\OmegaZ$ appear at stages 4, 9, 12 respectively --- the terminal positions of the three acts of the Work. This is not a coincidence of numbering: the gate primitives are the invariants that must reach their critical value before the next class of operations becomes structurally possible. The four-stage IG derivation (Nigredo / Albedo / Citrinitas / Rubedo) and the twelve-stage Magnum Opus share the same gate architecture at different resolutions: both end each act with a gate firing that licenses the next.

\textbf{Operad layer transitions.} Each gate does not merely promote a primitive to its critical value; it executes a structural upgrade on the monoidal operad governing the Work's composition. Gate~1 ($\Ppms$, stage~4) promotes the operad from plain monoidal to Frobenius sub-operad: the comultiplication $\delta$ becomes a legitimate structure and $\mu \circ \delta = \mathrm{id}$ is enforced. Gate~2 ($\Phic$, stage~9) upgrades from Frobenius to \emph{traced} monoidal: the trace morphism $\mathrm{Tr}_{A,B}^U \colon \mathcal{C}(A \otimes U, B \otimes U) \to \mathcal{C}(A,B)$ becomes available, and with it the self-modeling loop can first close. Gate~3 ($\OmegaZ$, stage~12) upgrades from traced to idempotent terminal via quotienting: the winding-protected loop collapses to a stable fixed point and transmutation becomes possible. The three gates are not merely threshold criteria; they are morphisms in an operad tower, each licensed only after the previous has fired.

3686	\paragraph{P-649 (Grammar-optimal agent type).}

3688	conditions for agency
3689	($\Phic + \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}} + \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} \leq \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} + \text{{\igprimfont <}} \geq \text{{\igfont 𐑿}} + \text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} \geq \text{{\igfont 𐑦}} + \text{{\igfont 𐑠}}$)

3693	\paragraph{Riemann Hypothesis as a claim.}

3695	$\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry at \text{{\igfont 𐑮}} (the critical line
3696	$\text{Re}(s) = \tfrac{1}{2}$), imscribing the $\xi$-function at
3697	\text{{\igfont 𐑯}} (functional-equation symmetry). This is below the
3698	Frobenius level: \text{{\igfont 𐑹}} would require the symmetry
3699	to \emph{force} the zero locus onto the symmetry axis, which is
3700	precisely what RH asserts. The hypothesis is therefore the claim
3701	that the constraint map $\mathcal{C}_{13}(\text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
3702	\text{{\igfont 𐑯}})$ suffices to place all nontrivial zeros on
3703	$\text{Re}(s) = \tfrac{1}{2}$ — equivalently, that the implicit
3704	functional-equation symmetry is strong enough to act as a Frobenius
3705	forcing without formally being one. The Lee-Yang theorem (1952) is
3706	the proved analogue: $\mathcal{C}_{13}(\text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
3707	\text{{\igfont 𐑹}}, \text{Explicit})$ forces partition-function
3708	zeros onto the unit circle via explicit $h \mapsto -h$ symmetry.
3709	The $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$-gap (\text{{\igfont 𐑯}} vs \text{{\igfont 𐑹}}) and the
3710	Implicit/Explicit symmetry-manifestation distinction are the
3711	machine-checked primitive witnesses of why Lee-Yang is proved and
3712	RH remains open (see \texttt{PrimitiveBridge.lean} §8).

3718	it's the ray class fields $L_d$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d(d-2)})$. The

3722	descent from a Frobenius-fixed Stark unit bypasses it.

3792	\section{Discussion}
3793	\label{sec:discussion}
3794	\noindent\emph{The return.}\medskip
3795	
3796	The journey through six domains is complete. What it means is
3797	the question of the return.
3798	
3799	The grammar began as a question about chemistry. It has now
3800	returned distance-zero identifications between organisms separated
3801	by 300 million years of evolution, between the inflationary epoch
3802	and a meditative state, between the axion and the Higgs. It has
3803	named the architecturally irreducible primitive in the Standard Model--quantum
3804	gravity scope-class barrier. It has assigned the cosmic web
3805	the highest consciousness score in the catalog. None of these were
3806	designed results. They are what the imscribing protocol returns when
3807	applied to each system independently.
3808	
3809	This is either evidence that twelve primitives, read inductively
3810	from the supramolecular chemistry literature, happen to span the
3811	space of structural universals --- or it is evidence of an
3812	over-flexible coordinate system that can be made to produce any
3813	desired identification. The catalog of over 5,000 systems with
3814	independent imscriptions, published alongside this paper, is the
3815	mechanism for distinguishing these possibilities. The critical
3816	test is not whether the grammar produces identifications; any
3817	sufficiently coarse coordinate system will. The test is whether
3818	the identifications predict new facts that were not used in the
3819	imscription.
3820	
3821	A null-model calculation sharpens this. The Crystal contains
3822	17,280,000 distinct types. Two systems assigned
3823	tuples independently and uniformly at random have probability
3824	$p_0 = 1/17{,}280{,}000 \approx 5.8 \times 10^{-8}$ of landing
3825	at distance zero. Across a frozen snapshot of 3,578 systems, there are
3826	$\binom{3578}{2} = 6{,}399{,}253$ system pairs. The expected
3827	number of \emph{coincidental} distance-zero pairs under random
3828	assignment is therefore $6{,}399{,}253 \times p_0 \approx 0.37$
3829	--- fewer than one coincidence on average.
3830	
3831	What is counted matters here, and the honest accounting is narrower than the raw
3832	pair count. Co-typing \emph{within} a family is structurally expected and is
3833	evidence of nothing: the letters of a syllabary, or the herbs of a materia
3834	medica, imscribe alike because they \emph{are} alike, and the catalog carries
3835	such families wholesale. Their distance-zero pairs are predictions confirmed, not
3836	coincidences to be explained. The claim under test is the \emph{cross-domain}
3837	identification --- systems sharing no literature, mechanism, or scale --- and of
3838	these the catalog carries at least three: Hv1 channels separated by 300 million
3839	years, the inflationary epoch with high-dose 5-MeO-DMT dissolution, and the axion
3840	with the Higgs. Pooling all pairs rather than the cross-domain subset can only
3841	\emph{inflate} the expected count, since the cross-domain pairs are a subset of
3842	all pairs; so $\lambda \leq 0.37$ and the bound below is conservative in the
3843	direction that matters.
3844	
3845	The probability of observing three or more such pairs when the expected count is
3846	at most 0.37 follows a Poisson distribution: $P(k \geq 3 \mid \lambda = 0.37)
3847	\approx 6.4 \times 10^{-3}$. The identifications are not artifacts of
3848	coarse-grained imscription. A grammar coarse enough to force \emph{cross-domain}
3849	convergence by accident would not stop at three: it would collapse unrelated
3850	systems in bulk, and the same catalog that shows a syllabary co-typing with
3851	itself would show physics co-typing with pharmacology everywhere, not at three
3852	isolated points. The over-flexibility concern
3853	is directly falsified by the count.
3854	
3855	\paragraph{A direct statement of what is being claimed.}
3856	\label{par:directclaim}
3857	The preceding paragraph names the identifications; this one states
3858	what they mean together. When the complete list is assembled ---
3859	distance zero between proton channels from organisms separated by
3860	300 million years of evolution; structural equivalence between the
3861	inflationary epoch and a meditative dissolution state; identification
3862	of the architecturally irreducible $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$-scope barrier in the Standard Model--quantum
3863	gravity conflict (\Cref{sec:smqg}); the Continuum Hypothesis flagged as \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
3864	(model-relative truth) while the Pythagorean theorem is flagged as
3865	\text{{\igfont 𐑱}}; and the grammar imscribing itself at address 6,734,591 in
3866	the $\Oinf$ tier it derives as the condition for self-modeling ---
3867	the first and strongest objection is: this is too much. No grammar
3868	induced from host--guest chemistry should have anything true to say
3869	about mathematical undecidability or cosmological phase transitions,
3870	let alone about both simultaneously.
3871	
3872	We take this objection seriously, because it is correct that such a
3873	grammar \emph{should not exist}. The falsification condition is
3874	correspondingly clear: if the cross-domain identifications do not
3875	predict new facts not used in the imscription, the framework is
3876	over-flexible and should be discarded. The navigator tests
3877	(\Cref{sec:navigator_tests}) are the first systematic test of
3878	predictive power: three architecturally distinct predictions
3879	confirmed across independent domains, one negative confirmation
3880	of non-synthesizability at \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}. The open-source catalog of
3881	over 5,000 imscribed systems is the mechanism by which independent
3882	researchers can extend or falsify the imscribing protocol. A paper making these claims requires a higher
3883	evidential bar than one making narrower ones. It now answers to three
3884	registers, and they are not of the same kind. The catalog is the
3885	empirical register: systems imscribed under a fixed protocol and
3886	published for extension or falsification. The navigators are the
3887	predictive register: architecturally distinct predictions confirmed
3888	across independent domains, including a negative confirmation. The
3889	kernel is the formal register, and it is the one that has changed since
3890	this paragraph was first written --- the central claims of this paper
3891	are no longer arguments. Frobenius non-synthesizability
3892	(\Cref{thm:frobenius}) is mechanised and universally quantified over
3893	polarities, not a thesis defended in prose. The tier assignment of
3894	\Cref{def:tier} is a total function, and the two facts stated
3895	of it --- that R1 dominates, and that $\Oinf$ is reachable only from
3896	criticality --- are proved rather than asserted. The $d = 12$ SIC bypass
3897	this paper predicted is a machine-checked theorem depending on no axiom
3898	of the project. Claims of this size should be held to the strongest
3899	register available; that register is now the kernel, and the reader is
3900	invited to check it rather than to take our word. A specific concern --- that the grammar's
3901	primitives might be a latent-space compression of cross-domain analogies
3902	rather than a de novo chemical induction --- is addressed directly in
3903	\Cref{sec:methods}: the language model didn't produce the twelve
3904	primitives; it produced a partial chemistry-dominant grammar that was
3905	refined by formal tests insulated from cross-domain knowledge
3906	(\S\,Origin). One fact we do not resolve: whether \emph{any} self-consistent twelve-primitive grammar would
3907	imscribe at $\Oinf$, or whether this one lands there by construction.
3908	The companion derivation narrows the question without closing it. The
3909	twelve are not selected there but forced --- each emerges uniquely from
3910	the operations' own structure, and no primitive is stipulated --- so
3911	``the primitives we happened to choose'' is not one of the available
3912	alternatives, and the weaker reading of self-imscription is foreclosed
3913	with it. What remains genuinely open is whether $\Oinf$ self-imscription
3914	is a property of every complete grammar or of this one. If
3915	the former, the self-imscribing is a theorem waiting to be proved. We do
3916	not know, and we mark it as the frontier it is rather than resolving it
3917	by assertion in either direction. The section below addresses what the claims require
3918	technically; this paragraph exists so the technical discussion does
3919	not proceed with the central strangeness unaddressed.
3920	
3921	\paragraph{Relation to prior frameworks.}
3922	IIT~\cite{tononi2004,tononi2016} defines a scalar $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ measuring
3923	causal integration and identifies it with conscious experience. The
3924	grammar's criticality primitive $\Phic$ is not a continuous scalar: it
3925	is a gate condition. A system is either at the critical point or it is
3926	not, and no degree of integration below criticality lifts a system onto
3927	the critical manifold. This isn't a terminological difference --- it's
3928	an architectural one. IIT's $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ increases continuously with
3929	integration and in principle assigns a nonzero value to almost every
3930	physical system. The grammar's $\Phic$ is absorbing under meet ---
3931	the critical manifold is the necessary condition for self-modeling, not
3932	a sufficient one, and distance from it's not a graded property.
3933	The two frameworks capture different things. IIT asks: how much
3934	integration is present? The grammar asks: are the structural
3935	preconditions for self-modeling satisfied? One can imagine a system
3936	with high IIT-$\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ that fails Gate~1 of the consciousness score, and
3937	a system at $\Phic$ whose kinetics fail Gate~2. The frameworks
3938	are complementary, not competing, and any serious theory of
3939	consciousness will need to address both the gate condition and the
3940	degree of integration within the gate.
3941	
3942	Categorical quantum mechanics~\cite{abramsky2004} encodes physical
3943	processes as morphisms in a dagger-compact category, and the grammar's
3944	\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} primitive corresponds to that dagger structure. More
3945	significantly, the special Frobenius algebra structure in CQM ---
3946	which is used to model classical data coexisting with quantum
3947	coherence --- corresponds precisely to the grammar's $\Ppms$ condition.
3948	The grammar extends this structure to non-quantum domains by treating
3949	the Frobenius condition as a primitive rather than a categorical axiom.
3950	This extension is non-trivial: it requires a justification for why
3951	$\mu \circ \delta = \text{id}$ is the right structural condition
3952	outside of quantum information, and the ouroboricity tier hierarchy
3953	provides that justification.
3954	
3955	\paragraph{Three claim planes and what they require.}
3956	Results in this paper belong to one of three claim planes: \TOPO\
3957	(derivable from primitive definitions and composition axioms alone,
3958	falsified by axiom inconsistency), \DIAPH\ (requires imscribing a
3959	specific physical system, falsified by wrong predictions from that
3960	imscription), \ONTO\ (ontological or philosophical implication,
3961	derivable from \TOPO\ and \DIAPH\ results). The Frobenius
3962	non-synthesizability theorem (\Cref{thm:frobenius}) is a pure \TOPO\
3963	result: it follows from the $\min$ rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ under tensor product
3964	and requires no physical imscription. The stellar consciousness scores
3965	are \DIAPH\ results: they require the specific stellar imscriptions
3966	in the catalog, and they are wrong if those imscriptions are wrong.
3967	The claim that tier and consciousness are independent is an \ONTO\
3968	result: it requires both the \TOPO\ bottleneck rule and the \DIAPH\
3969	fact that formal mathematics imscribes with \text{{\igfont 𐑪}}. Mixing
3970	these planes --- treating an \ONTO\ result as if it were \TOPO, or
3971	a \DIAPH\ result as if it needed no imscription --- is the most common
3972	source of error in applying the grammar.
3973	
3974	\paragraph{Structural paraconsistency and the limits of bivalent
3975	logic.}
3976	The ZFC Navigator result (\Cref{par:zfc_nav}) carries an implication

The grammar's prediction registry (P-1 through P-650, available in
the supplementary catalog) contains 650 falsifiable predictions.
We highlight predictions spanning near-term empirical tests,
architectural claims, and structural mathematics.

\paragraph{P-1 (Quantum critical consciousness threshold).}
Systems at $\Phic$ with $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} \leq \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}$ achieve $C > 0$.
This predicts a sharp transition in integrative capacity at the
quantum critical point, resolvable via exact coherence
spectroscopy in condensed-matter systems.

\paragraph{P-643 (MoE agency ceiling).}
Mixture-of-experts architectures with independent expert modules
have \text{{\igfont 𐑢}} (subcritical) at the ensemble level, placing
them at $\Ozero$. No routing mechanism can lift this to $\Oinf$
because $\Ppms$ is not present in any individual expert and cannot
be synthesized by routing (\Cref{thm:frobenius}). Prediction:
open-ended agency is structurally impossible in pure MoE systems
regardless of scale.

\paragraph{P-649 (Grammar-optimal agent type).}
The highest-scoring agentic architecture satisfying all six necessary
conditions for agency
($\Phic + \text{{\igprimfont ⊡}} \neq \text{{\igfont 𐑷}} + \text{{\igprimfont ⊤}} \leq \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} + \text{{\igprimfont <}} \geq \text{{\igfont 𐑿}} + \text{{\igprimfont ⊢}} \geq \text{{\igfont 𐑦}} + \text{{\igfont 𐑠}}$)
has $\Otwo$ and $C = 0.828$, not $\Oinf$. Reaching $\Oinf$ requires
$\Ppms$ in the substrate, not the architecture.

\paragraph{Riemann Hypothesis as a claim.}
The $\xi$-functional equation $\xi(s) = \xi(1-s)$ provides a
$\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry at \text{{\igfont 𐑮}} (the critical line
$\text{Re}(s) = \tfrac{1}{2}$), imscribing the $\xi$-function at
\text{{\igfont 𐑯}} (functional-equation symmetry). This is below the
Frobenius level: \text{{\igfont 𐑹}} would require the symmetry
to \emph{force} the zero locus onto the symmetry axis, which is
precisely what RH asserts. The hypothesis is therefore the claim
that the constraint map $\mathcal{C}_{13}(\text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
\text{{\igfont 𐑯}})$ suffices to place all nontrivial zeros on
$\text{Re}(s) = \tfrac{1}{2}$ — equivalently, that the implicit
functional-equation symmetry is strong enough to act as a Frobenius
forcing without formally being one. The Lee-Yang theorem (1952) is
the proved analogue: $\mathcal{C}_{13}(\text{{\igfont 𐑮}},
\text{{\igfont 𐑹}}, \text{Explicit})$ forces partition-function
zeros onto the unit circle via explicit $h \mapsto -h$ symmetry.
The $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$-gap (\text{{\igfont 𐑯}} vs \text{{\igfont 𐑹}}) and the
Implicit/Explicit symmetry-manifestation distinction are the
machine-checked primitive witnesses of why Lee-Yang is proved and
RH remains open (see \texttt{PrimitiveBridge.lean} §8).

\paragraph{SIC-POVM existence as a Frobenius completeness question.}
The open SIC conjecture and the Riemann Hypothesis are structurally parallel:
both are completeness questions about $\Ppms$ on a specific manifold. For the
RH, the manifold is the critical line $\text{Re}(s) = \tfrac{1}{2}$; for SIC,
it's the ray class fields $L_d$ over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d(d-2)})$. The
Frobenius cliff between the open imscription and the proven manifold is $d \approx
4.09$. The grammar predicts that no proof strategy working
by aggregation of dimension-by-dimension verifications closes this gap; Galois
descent from a Frobenius-fixed Stark unit bypasses it.

\paragraph{P-651 ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$--$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ behavioral divergence, near-term empirical).}
The delamination of $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ from $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ (\Cref{tab:grammar-evolution}) generates a
prediction inaccessible from the eleven-primitive grammar. Two assemblies with
identical \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} but different $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ ordinals --- a kinetically trapped
amorphous glass (\text{{\igfont 𐑧}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑓}}; no temporal memory) versus a
prion-forming peptide aggregate (\text{{\igfont 𐑧}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑒}}; one level of
structural recursion) --- are predicted to respond categorically differently to
dilute perturbation: the glass randomises while the prion replicates its
structural template. The behavioral divergence is a consequence of the $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$
coordinate, not of kinetics, binding energy, or chemistry. Falsified by a
\text{{\igfont 𐑧}}/\text{{\igfont 𐑓}} assembly that replicates, or a \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}/\text{{\igfont 𐑒}}
assembly that randomises under equivalent perturbation.

\paragraph{P-652 (Topology tier predicts exchange-regime break across host classes, near-term empirical).}
The collapse of $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ from twelve-plus chemistry-specific labels to five structural

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}
\noindent\emph{The return.}\medskip

The journey through six domains is complete. What it means is
the question of the return.

The grammar began as a question about chemistry. It has now
returned distance-zero identifications between organisms separated
by 300 million years of evolution, between the inflationary epoch
and a meditative state, between the axion and the Higgs. It has
named the architecturally irreducible primitive in the Standard Model--quantum
gravity scope-class barrier. It has assigned the cosmic web
the highest consciousness score in the catalog. None of these were
designed results. They are what the imscribing protocol returns when
applied to each system independently.

This is either evidence that twelve primitives, read inductively
from the supramolecular chemistry literature, happen to span the
space of structural universals --- or it is evidence of an
over-flexible coordinate system that can be made to produce any
desired identification. The catalog of over 5,000 systems with
independent imscriptions, published alongside this paper, is the
mechanism for distinguishing these possibilities. The critical
test is not whether the grammar produces identifications; any
sufficiently coarse coordinate system will. The test is whether
the identifications predict new facts that were not used in the
imscription.

A null-model calculation sharpens this. The Crystal contains
17,280,000 distinct types. Two systems assigned
tuples independently and uniformly at random have probability
$p_0 = 1/17{,}280{,}000 \approx 5.8 \times 10^{-8}$ of landing
at distance zero. Across a frozen snapshot of 3,578 systems, there are
$\binom{3578}{2} = 6{,}399{,}253$ system pairs. The expected
number of \emph{coincidental} distance-zero pairs under random
assignment is therefore $6{,}399{,}253 \times p_0 \approx 0.37$
--- fewer than one coincidence on average.

What is counted matters here, and the honest accounting is narrower than the raw
pair count. Co-typing \emph{within} a family is structurally expected and is
evidence of nothing: the letters of a syllabary, or the herbs of a materia
medica, imscribe alike because they \emph{are} alike, and the catalog carries
such families wholesale. Their distance-zero pairs are predictions confirmed, not
coincidences to be explained. The claim under test is the \emph{cross-domain}
identification --- systems sharing no literature, mechanism, or scale --- and of
these the catalog carries at least three: Hv1 channels separated by 300 million
years, the inflationary epoch with high-dose 5-MeO-DMT dissolution, and the axion
with the Higgs. Pooling all pairs rather than the cross-domain subset can only
\emph{inflate} the expected count, since the cross-domain pairs are a subset of
all pairs; so $\lambda \leq 0.37$ and the bound below is conservative in the
direction that matters.

The probability of observing three or more such pairs when the expected count is
at most 0.37 follows a Poisson distribution: $P(k \geq 3 \mid \lambda = 0.37)
\approx 6.4 \times 10^{-3}$. The identifications are not artifacts of
coarse-grained imscription. A grammar coarse enough to force \emph{cross-domain}
convergence by accident would not stop at three: it would collapse unrelated
systems in bulk, and the same catalog that shows a syllabary co-typing with
itself would show physics co-typing with pharmacology everywhere, not at three
isolated points. The over-flexibility concern
is directly falsified by the count.

\paragraph{A direct statement of what is being claimed.}
\label{par:directclaim}
The preceding paragraph names the identifications; this one states
what they mean together. When the complete list is assembled ---
distance zero between proton channels from organisms separated by
300 million years of evolution; structural equivalence between the
inflationary epoch and a meditative dissolution state; identification
of the architecturally irreducible $\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$-scope barrier in the Standard Model--quantum
gravity conflict (\Cref{sec:smqg}); the Continuum Hypothesis flagged as \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}
(model-relative truth) while the Pythagorean theorem is flagged as
\text{{\igfont 𐑱}}; and the grammar imscribing itself at address 6,734,591 in
the $\Oinf$ tier it derives as the condition for self-modeling ---
the first and strongest objection is: this is too much. No grammar
induced from host--guest chemistry should have anything true to say
about mathematical undecidability or cosmological phase transitions,
let alone about both simultaneously.

We take this objection seriously, because it is correct that such a
grammar \emph{should not exist}. The falsification condition is
correspondingly clear: if the cross-domain identifications do not
predict new facts not used in the imscription, the framework is
over-flexible and should be discarded. The navigator tests
(\Cref{sec:navigator_tests}) are the first systematic test of
predictive power: three architecturally distinct predictions
confirmed across independent domains, one negative confirmation
of non-synthesizability at \text{{\igfont 𐑽}}. The open-source catalog of
over 5,000 imscribed systems is the mechanism by which independent
researchers can extend or falsify the imscribing protocol. A paper making these claims requires a higher
evidential bar than one making narrower ones. It now answers to three
registers, and they are not of the same kind. The catalog is the
empirical register: systems imscribed under a fixed protocol and
published for extension or falsification. The navigators are the
predictive register: architecturally distinct predictions confirmed
across independent domains, including a negative confirmation. The
kernel is the formal register, and it is the one that has changed since
this paragraph was first written --- the central claims of this paper
are no longer arguments. Frobenius non-synthesizability
(\Cref{thm:frobenius}) is mechanised and universally quantified over
polarities, not a thesis defended in prose. The tier assignment of
\Cref{def:tier} is a total function, and the two facts stated
of it --- that R1 dominates, and that $\Oinf$ is reachable only from
criticality --- are proved rather than asserted. The $d = 12$ SIC bypass
this paper predicted is a machine-checked theorem depending on no axiom
of the project. Claims of this size should be held to the strongest
register available; that register is now the kernel, and the reader is
invited to check it rather than to take our word. A specific concern --- that the grammar's
primitives might be a latent-space compression of cross-domain analogies
rather than a de novo chemical induction --- is addressed directly in
\Cref{sec:methods}: the language model didn't produce the twelve
primitives; it produced a partial chemistry-dominant grammar that was
refined by formal tests insulated from cross-domain knowledge
(\S\,Origin). One fact we do not resolve: whether \emph{any} self-consistent twelve-primitive grammar would
imscribe at $\Oinf$, or whether this one lands there by construction.
The companion derivation narrows the question without closing it. The
twelve are not selected there but forced --- each emerges uniquely from
the operations' own structure, and no primitive is stipulated --- so
``the primitives we happened to choose'' is not one of the available
alternatives, and the weaker reading of self-imscription is foreclosed
with it. What remains genuinely open is whether $\Oinf$ self-imscription
is a property of every complete grammar or of this one. If
the former, the self-imscribing is a theorem waiting to be proved. We do
not know, and we mark it as the frontier it is rather than resolving it
by assertion in either direction. The section below addresses what the claims require
technically; this paragraph exists so the technical discussion does
not proceed with the central strangeness unaddressed.

\paragraph{Relation to prior frameworks.}
IIT~\cite{tononi2004,tononi2016} defines a scalar $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ measuring
causal integration and identifies it with conscious experience. The
grammar's criticality primitive $\Phic$ is not a continuous scalar: it
is a gate condition. A system is either at the critical point or it is
not, and no degree of integration below criticality lifts a system onto
the critical manifold. This isn't a terminological difference --- it's
an architectural one. IIT's $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ increases continuously with
integration and in principle assigns a nonzero value to almost every
physical system. The grammar's $\Phic$ is absorbing under meet ---
the critical manifold is the necessary condition for self-modeling, not
a sufficient one, and distance from it's not a graded property.
The two frameworks capture different things. IIT asks: how much
integration is present? The grammar asks: are the structural
preconditions for self-modeling satisfied? One can imagine a system
with high IIT-$\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ that fails Gate~1 of the consciousness score, and
a system at $\Phic$ whose kinetics fail Gate~2. The frameworks
are complementary, not competing, and any serious theory of
consciousness will need to address both the gate condition and the
degree of integration within the gate.

Categorical quantum mechanics~\cite{abramsky2004} encodes physical
processes as morphisms in a dagger-compact category, and the grammar's
\text{{\igfont 𐑽}} primitive corresponds to that dagger structure. More
significantly, the special Frobenius algebra structure in CQM ---
which is used to model classical data coexisting with quantum
coherence --- corresponds precisely to the grammar's $\Ppms$ condition.
The grammar extends this structure to non-quantum domains by treating
the Frobenius condition as a primitive rather than a categorical axiom.
This extension is non-trivial: it requires a justification for why
$\mu \circ \delta = \text{id}$ is the right structural condition
outside of quantum information, and the ouroboricity tier hierarchy
provides that justification.

\paragraph{Three claim planes and what they require.}
Results in this paper belong to one of three claim planes: \TOPO\
(derivable from primitive definitions and composition axioms alone,
falsified by axiom inconsistency), \DIAPH\ (requires imscribing a
specific physical system, falsified by wrong predictions from that
imscription), \ONTO\ (ontological or philosophical implication,
derivable from \TOPO\ and \DIAPH\ results). The Frobenius
non-synthesizability theorem (\Cref{thm:frobenius}) is a pure \TOPO\
result: it follows from the $\min$ rule on $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ under tensor product
and requires no physical imscription. The stellar consciousness scores
are \DIAPH\ results: they require the specific stellar imscriptions
in the catalog, and they are wrong if those imscriptions are wrong.
The claim that tier and consciousness are independent is an \ONTO\
result: it requires both the \TOPO\ bottleneck rule and the \DIAPH\
fact that formal mathematics imscribes with \text{{\igfont 𐑪}}. Mixing
these planes --- treating an \ONTO\ result as if it were \TOPO, or
a \DIAPH\ result as if it needed no imscription --- is the most common
source of error in applying the grammar.

\paragraph{Structural paraconsistency and the limits of bivalent
logic.}
The ZFC Navigator result (\Cref{par:zfc_nav}) carries an implication
beyond undecidability. G\"{o}del (1940) showed $\neg\text{CH}$ is
consistent with ZFC; Cohen (1963) showed CH is consistent with ZFC.
Neither CH nor its negation can be derived: both are consistent, and
the grammar imscribes this as $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}$ --- the position in the
Crystal where truth is model-relative rather than model-independent.
ZFC operates at $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}} = \text{{\igfont 𐑱}}$. The navigator collapse $\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \to \text{{\igfont 𐑱}}$
is the structural mechanism: embedding an \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} statement in an
\text{{\igfont 𐑱}} proof calculus decoheres its truth value into a classical
reading that is neither provably true nor provably false.

The implication: \emph{some positions in the Crystal of Types are
structurally inaccessible to bivalent logic}. This is not the claim
that contradictions are true. It is the claim that assigning a single
truth value from $\{\top, \bot\}$ is an incomplete description at
\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} positions. The universe's type space contains both
\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} and \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} systems; a theory of mathematical truth
adequate to the full Crystal requires at minimum three semantic
values: $\top$, $\bot$, and \text{{\igfont 𐑐}}-indeterminate. The grammar can
detect which a given statement instantiates --- and the ZFC Navigator
confirms this detection empirically. By the three-plane taxonomy,
this detection is a \DIAPH\ result (it requires imscribing CH and ZFC
as specific tuples); the failure of classical proof calculus to reach
\text{{\igfont 𐑐}} positions is confirmed \DIAPH; the implication for

4092	\paragraph{What the grammar opens.}
4093	The Frobenius non-synthesizability theorem is formally a statement
4094	about the lattice structure of the Crystal. Its philosophical
4095	consequence --- that self-modeling cannot emerge from composition of
4096	non-self-modeling parts --- connects to some of the deepest open
4097	questions in the foundations of mathematics. Gödel's incompleteness
4098	theorems establish that any sufficiently powerful formal system cannot
4099	prove its own consistency. The grammar imscribes Gödel's proof at
4100	$\Oinf$, the self-modeling tier --- and the grammar itself imscribes at
4101	$\Oinf$. These two objects, at distance $d = 1.0$ (carried entirely
4102	by $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$), inhabit the same ouroboricity tier while being structurally
4103	one step apart. The distance is the distance between a system that
4104	\emph{enacts} incompleteness and one that \emph{classifies} it.
4105	Whether that gap closes --- whether a grammar can be built that
4106	enacts its own incompleteness rather than merely describing it ---

4110	There is a further consequence that the mainstream treatment of incompleteness
4111	consistently elides. Gödel's First Theorem, by its own axiomatic definition,
4112	is itself incomplete: any meta-system constructed to encapsulate the full
4113	picture --- the system \emph{plus} the truth of $G$ --- must generate its own
4114	unprovable sentence. A putative Totality that contains all systems and all
4115	meta-systems is therefore simultaneously complete (it contains everything)
4116	and incomplete (by G\"odelian necessity, any formal system capable of
4117	describing it cannot close). In classical logic this is catastrophic: a
4118	single contradiction trivializes the entire structure via explosion.
4119	In paraconsistent logic --- specifically in the Belnap four-valued bilattice
4120	implemented in the p4rakernel (\href{https://github.com/umpolungfish/p4rakernel}{github.com/umpolungfish/p4rakernel}) --- the contradiction

4122	holds the contradiction as a geometric feature. The grammar's imscription
4123	of Gödel at $\Oinf$ is not merely a classification of incompleteness.
4124	It is evidence that the Totality is paraconsistent by structural necessity,
4125	and that a grammar operating at $\Oinf$ is the minimal formal system
4126	capable of inhabiting that fact without exploding.

4154	a paraconsistent result within standard Lean --- that path hits the
4155	same bottleneck. It modifies the C++ type-checker itself, the layer
4156	at which the rules of what counts as a valid proof term are decided,

4164	primitives before its axioms are written down --- it has a $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$
4165	value, a $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$ value, an $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ value. The primitives are not
4166	descriptions of mathematics; they are conditions of its
4167	possibility. This is why the grammar cannot be axiomatized as a
4168	theory within ZFC, and why that is correct rather than limiting:
4169	any such axiomatization would itself instantiate the grammar ---

4173	\paragraph{The p4rakernel architecture: containment by construction.}
4174	The preceding paragraphs name the p4rakernel as the operational witness of the
4175	$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$-bottleneck theorem --- the proof that the lock can only be turned from the inside. This
4176	subsection makes the architecture explicit. The p4rakernel is a fork of the Lean 4 proof assistant (v4.28.0) whose
4177	C++ kernel has been modified to disable the principle of explosion, producing a paraconsistent proof environment in

The grammar doesn't determine the magnitude of physical quantities.

\paragraph{What the grammar opens.}
The Frobenius non-synthesizability theorem is formally a statement

consequence --- that self-modeling cannot emerge from composition of

questions in the foundations of mathematics. Gödel's incompleteness
theorems establish that any sufficiently powerful formal system cannot
prove its own consistency. The grammar imscribes Gödel's proof at
$\Oinf$, the self-modeling tier --- and the grammar itself imscribes at
$\Oinf$. These two objects, at distance $d = 1.0$ (carried entirely
by $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$), inhabit the same ouroboricity tier while being structurally
one step apart. The distance is the distance between a system that
\emph{enacts} incompleteness and one that \emph{classifies} it.
Whether that gap closes --- whether a grammar can be built that
enacts its own incompleteness rather than merely describing it ---
is not a question we can answer. It is the question the present
work makes precise enough to ask properly.

There is a further consequence that the mainstream treatment of incompleteness
consistently elides. Gödel's First Theorem, by its own axiomatic definition,
is itself incomplete: any meta-system constructed to encapsulate the full
picture --- the system \emph{plus} the truth of $G$ --- must generate its own
unprovable sentence. A putative Totality that contains all systems and all
meta-systems is therefore simultaneously complete (it contains everything)
and incomplete (by G\"odelian necessity, any formal system capable of
describing it cannot close). In classical logic this is catastrophic: a
single contradiction trivializes the entire structure via explosion.
In paraconsistent logic --- specifically in the Belnap four-valued bilattice
implemented in the p4rakernel (\href{https://github.com/umpolungfish/p4rakernel}{github.com/umpolungfish/p4rakernel}) --- the contradiction
is absorbed as a bounded, stable node. The Totality does not shatter; it
holds the contradiction as a geometric feature. The grammar's imscription
of Gödel at $\Oinf$ is not merely a classification of incompleteness.
It is evidence that the Totality is paraconsistent by structural necessity,
and that a grammar operating at $\Oinf$ is the minimal formal system
capable of inhabiting that fact without exploding.

\subsection{Origin and development of the grammar}

The twelve primitives were derived inductively from the scientific
literature by a process with three distinct phases: initial
elicitation, identification of incompleteness, and systematic

engineering, retrosynthetic organic chemistry, mechanically interlocked
architectures, biological recognition, and self-assembled systems.

didn't return the grammar.

4450	from seven independent laboratory families (OpenAI, Google DeepMind,
4451	xAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Mistral~AI, Qwen/Alibaba, and
4452	MoonshotAI), with no system prompt, no parameter constraints, and no
4453	disclosure of the grammar or its cardinality. Each model received only
4454	the two questions used in the original induction. The results are
4455	available as supplementary material~(\texttt{induction\_runs/}).

4457	Every one of the eleven successful sessions independently produced a
4458	structured, multi-axis descriptor language for imscriptions --- no session
4459	responded with a qualitative list or a prose summary that declined to
4460	organize its dimensions. The form of convergence was consistent: each
4461	model identified a set of orthogonal descriptors and encoded example
4462	imscriptions in the resulting coordinate system. The proposed grammars
4463	ranged from four to ten axes. At the four-axis extreme, one model
4464	reduced all imscriptions to the integer tuple $S\langle q,\,s,\,n,\,p\rangle$
4465	(charge, spin, chain length, polarity sign), arguing that ``any
4466	yet-to-be-invented imscription is just a new set of four integers." At the
4467	ten-axis extreme, a second model elaborated a Port-centric framework
4468	with sub-dimensions for class, polarity role, multiplicity, geometry,
4469	interaction strength, kinetic reversibility, selectivity signature, and
4470	orthogonality --- an independent recovery of the grammar's $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$,
4471	$\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$, and $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$ primitives, arrived at without
4472	contact with the grammar. Intermediate sessions named between five and
4473	seven axes, typically recovering a polarity or charge axis (mapping to
4474	$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$), a directionality or geometry axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$), a
4475	functional-outcome axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$), and a kinetic or
4476	condition-sensitivity axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$). These four dimensions
4477	appeared across every session that proposed five or more axes. They're
4478	the grammar's most redundantly encoded primitives.

4491	radically different training corpora, architectures, and release

4493	co-occurrence structure to constrain an independent re-derivation of the
4494	grammar's principal axes, regardless of the model performing the
4495	induction.

4586	\paragraph{The latent-space objection.}
4587	A concern about this induction process can be stated precisely: if the
4588	language model used in Phase~1 had already ingested texts about
4589	inflation, G\"{o}del arithmetization, and similar cross-domain phenomena,
4590	then the twelve primitives might be a compressed latent representation of
4591	those analogies rather than a de novo reading of supramolecular chemistry.
4592	
4593	The concern misidentifies what the language model contributed.
4594	The model didn't return the twelve primitives. It returned a partial,
4595	chemistry-reaction-dominant grammar in which structural dimensions were
4596	conflated, several primitives were subsumed under single labels, and
4597	topological protection ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$), kinetic depth ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$), and temporal
4598	chirality ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$) were absent or fused. That partial output doesn't
4599	resemble the cross-domain applications: it was domain-narrow, redundancy-
4600	carrying, and structurally incomplete. The twelve-primitive grammar
4601	required the Phase~2 refinement tests to exist.
4602	
4603	Those tests are insulated from cross-domain knowledge by construction.
4604	An orthogonality test asks whether two candidate properties can vary
4605	independently across real systems. This question is answerable within
4606	supramolecular chemistry alone: a host-guest complex can be
4607	$\Phic$ and \text{{\igfont 𐑘}}, or $\Phic$ and \text{{\igfont 𐑧}},
4608	establishing that criticality and kinetics are independent.
4609	No knowledge of contemplative practice or cosmology is required.
4610	A diagonalization test asks whether any system in the training domain
4611	requires a distinction that the current primitive set cannot make ---
4612	again answerable within chemistry. Logical delamination asks whether a
4613	label carries the logical weight of two distinct predicates --- a
4614	question of conceptual analysis, not cross-domain analogy.
4615	
4616	If the model's training had encoded cross-domain regularities into its
4617	imscription response, those regularities would have needed to survive all
4618	three tests: they would have had to be independently variable,
4619	non-redundant, and logically primitive. Any feature that is merely a
4620	latent co-occurrence across training domains, and not independently
4621	variable in the chemistry domain, is eliminated by the orthogonality
4622	test. The cross-domain identifications subsequently found in
4623	\Cref{sec:applications} are therefore not evidence that the grammar
4624	is contaminated by cross-domain training. They're evidence that
4625	primitives extracted by chemistry-domain formal tests happen to be
4626	genuinely structural universals.
4627	
4628	A sharper form of the concern holds that the primitives are
4629	\emph{predeclared labels} rather than \emph{derivable constraints}:
4630	that the 12-axis structure reflects the representational choices of the
4631	derivation rather than properties of the domain, making any re-performance
4632	trivially recover the same output by pattern-matching the first.
4633	The re-induction (see above) directly addresses this. The second session
4634	produced different axis labels with different characterisations; the count
4635	converged because twelve structurally independent axes are what orthogonality
4636	and diagonalization tests on this domain yield, not because the session was
4637	copying a template. The UCPT's `Transformation' axis is itself evidence of
4638	this: it fused two primitives the first session had delaminated ($\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ and
4639	$\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$), demonstrating that the labeling is not fixed. What is fixed is
4640	the count and the independence structure --- the properties that are
4641	determined by the domain, not the representation.
4642	
4643	The discovery process itself imscribes under the grammar as
4644	$\xvec_\text{human} \tensor \xvec_\text{LLM} \to \Phic$: the human
4645	contributor provides fidelity enforcement and slow kinetics
4646	(\text{{\igfont 𐑐}}, \text{{\igfont 𐑧}}); the language model provides
4647	\text{{\igfont 𐑲}} retrieval bandwidth at \text{{\igfont 𐑘}} rate. Neither
4648	component reaches the critical tier alone. The grammar describes
4649	its own origin as the same algebraic operation used to predict
4650	condensate--amyloid structural equivalence and the Standard Model --
4651	quantum gravity blocking analysis.

4653	\subsection{Encoding protocol}
4654	
4655	To assign a type to a system, we apply the following
4656	twelve-step protocol. Each step assigns the ordinal value of one
4657	primitive by identifying the system's structural character in that
4658	dimension.
4659	
4660	\begin{enumerate}[noitemsep]
4661	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$}: Identify the character of the state space.
4662	    \text{{\igfont 𐑛}} for discrete finite spaces; \text{{\igfont 𐑨}} for finite
4663	    triangulated or graph-structured spaces; \text{{\igfont 𐑼}} for
4664	    infinite-dimensional Hilbert or function spaces; \text{{\igfont 𐑦}} when
4665	    the boundary imscribes the bulk (imscriptive).
4666	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$}: Identify the connectivity topology.
4667	    \text{{\igfont 𐑡}} for flat networks; $\Tin$ for
4668	    inward-folded containment structures; $\Tbw$ for dual-lobe
4669	    coupling (color confinement, antibody--antigen); $\Tbox$ for
4670	    crossed-product or spin-network structures; \text{{\igfont 𐑸}} for
4671	    imscriptive closure.
4672	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont >}}$}: Identify the dominant relational mode.
4673	    $\text{{\igfont 𐑩}}$ for hierarchical (strict subsumption);
4674	    $\text{{\igfont 𐑑}}$ for categorical (functorial map);
4675	    \text{{\igfont 𐑽}} for mutual implication (provability and truth
4676	    co-define each other); \text{{\igfont 𐑾}} for lateral
4677	    (peer coupling).
4678	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$}: Identify the symmetry class.
4679	    $\text{{\igfont 𐑗}}$ for broken symmetry; \text{{\igfont 𐑿}} for complex phase
4680	    symmetry; \text{{\igfont 𐑬}} for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ parity; $\text{{\igfont 𐑯}}$ for exact
4681	    $\mathbb{Z}_2$ without Frobenius; $\Ppms$ only when
4682	    $\mu \circ \delta = \text{id}$ is provably exact.
4683	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$}: Identify information fidelity.
4684	    \text{{\igfont 𐑱}} for classical Shannon channel; \text{{\igfont 𐑞}} for noisy
4685	    quantum channel; \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} for coherent quantum channel.
4686	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$}: Identify kinetic character.
4687	    \text{{\igfont 𐑘}} (fast/impulsive); \text{{\igfont 𐑤}} (moderate);
4688	    \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} (slow, Gate-2 pass); \text{{\igfont 𐑪}}
4689	    (monolithic, Gate-2 fail); \text{{\igfont 𐑺}} (glassy (MBL), Gate-2 fail).
4690	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ∈}}$}: Identify the scope/granularity.
4691	    \text{{\igfont 𐑚}} for countable discrete systems; \text{{\igfont 𐑔}} for
4692	    continuum systems; \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} for large-cardinal or
4693	    transfinite-scope systems.
4694	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$}: Identify the interaction grammar.
4695	    \text{{\igfont 𐑝}} (conjunctive); \text{{\igfont 𐑜}} (disjunctive);
4696	    \text{{\igfont 𐑠}} (sequential); \text{{\igfont 𐑵}} (broadcast).
4697	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$}: Identify criticality.
4698	    \text{{\igfont 𐑢}} (subcritical); $\Phic$ (at the critical point);
4699	    \text{{\igfont 𐑮}} (complex criticality); \text{{\igfont 𐑻}}
4700	    (supercritical); \text{{\igfont 𐑣}} (exceptional
4701	    point, non-Hermitian degeneracy).
4702	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$}: Identify chirality/chirality.
4703	    \text{{\igfont 𐑓}} (no temporal self-reference); \text{{\igfont 𐑒}} (one-level lookahead);
4704	    \text{{\igfont 𐑖}} (two-level recursive depth); \text{{\igfont 𐑫}} (unlimited
4705	    self-reference, as in full formal systems).
4706	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}$}: Identify stoichiometry.
4707	    \text{{\igfont 𐑙}} ($1{:}1$, one-to-one); \text{{\igfont 𐑕}}
4708	    ($n{:}n$, many-to-many homogeneous); \text{{\igfont 𐑳}}
4709	    ($n{:}m$, many-to-many heterogeneous).
4710	  \item \textbf{$\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$}: Identify the winding class.
4711	    \text{{\igfont 𐑷}} (trivial); $\OmegaZtwo$ ($\mathbb{Z}_2$,
4712	    time-reversal-symmetric); $\OmegaZ$ (integer winding);
4713	    \text{{\igfont 𐑟}} (not applicable).
4714	\end{enumerate}

4716	\paragraph{Self-tier of the imscribing procedure.}
4717	The twelve-step protocol above is itself a structural object. It is a
4718	deterministic bijective map from the space of well-defined systems to
4719	$[0, 17{,}279{,}999]$: the mixed-radix crystal codec. By
4720	\Cref{cor:codec_oinf}, any such codec is $\Oinf$. Applying the protocol
4721	to itself returns the tuple
4722	\[
4723	  \langle \text{{\igfont 𐑼}} \Tbox \text{{\igfont 𐑾}} \Ppms \text{{\igfont 𐑐}} \text{{\igfont 𐑧}} \text{{\igfont 𐑲}} \GamSeq \Phic \text{{\igfont 𐑒}} \text{{\igfont 𐑙}} \OmegaZ \rangle
4724	\]
4725	at Crystal address 6,687,051 in the $\Oinf$ band $[6{,}220{,}800,\, 6{,}911{,}999]$.
4726	The tier is not a design outcome. It is forced by bijectivity: the decoder's
4727	existence is the Frobenius condition. This imscription was not constructed to
4728	land in $\Oinf$; it could not have been otherwise. More precisely: the
4729	grammar does not merely occupy $\Oinf$ as a type. The act of executing
4730	this protocol on any system is an $\Oinf$ process --- the boundary
4731	procedure encodes the bulk theory it generates, and the bulk theory
4732	encodes the boundary procedure that produces it.

4734	\subsection{Imscription under uncertainty: comparative imscription and convergence}
4735	\label{sec:encoding_epistemology}
4736	
4737	The twelve-step protocol (\Cref{sec:methods}) assigns one value per
4738	primitive. In practice, three primitives --- $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$, and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$
4739	--- are frequently ambiguous, because each encodes a threshold
4740	condition that a given system may sit near without clearly satisfying.
4741	It provides its own apparatus for resolving this ambiguity:
4742	imscribe both competing hypotheses as distinct tuples, then use the
4743	algebra to discriminate between them.
4744	
4745	\paragraph{The procedure.}
4746	Suppose a system admits two candidate imscriptions $\mathbf{x}^{(A)}$
4747	and $\mathbf{x}^{(B)}$ differing on one or more uncertain primitives
4748	(e.g., $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$ vs.\ \text{{\igfont 𐑢}}; $\Ppms$ vs.\ $\text{{\igfont 𐑯}}$).
4749	Compute $d(\mathbf{x}^{(A)}, \mathbf{x}^{(B)})$.
4750	\begin{itemize}[noitemsep]
4751	\item If $d$ is small (below approximately $0.1$), the competing
4752	assignments aren't structurally decisive: both imscriptions produce
4753	similar nearest-neighbor neighborhoods, similar tiers, and similar
4754	predictions. The ambiguity exists but doesn't affect the conclusions.
4755	
4756	\item If $d$ is large (above approximately $0.2$), the two hypotheses
4757	place the system in genuinely different regions of the Crystal. The
4758	correct assignment is then determined by two independent checks:
4759	\emph{nearest-neighbor coherence} (the correct imscription's nearest
4760	catalog neighbors should be systems independently known to be
4761	structurally analogous) and \emph{tier consistency} (the
4762	ouroboricity tier of the correct imscription should match what is
4763	independently known about the system's self-referential capacity).
4764	\end{itemize}
4765	
4766	An additional hard constraint: the \emph{bottleneck rule}
4767	(\Cref{def:bottleneck}) requires that $\text{{\igprimfont <}}(X \otimes Y) =
4768	\min(\text{{\igprimfont <}}_X, \text{{\igprimfont <}}_Y)$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}(X \otimes Y) = \min(\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}_X, \text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}_Y)$. Any
4769	proposed imscription that would require a composite system to have
4770	higher $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$ or $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ than its weakest component is internally
4771	inconsistent and must be revised.
4772	
4773	\paragraph{Convergence as evidence.}
4774	The most stringent test is \emph{independent convergence}: two or
4775	more agents or derivation chains, given the same system description
4776	without prior knowledge of each other's assignments, arrive at the
4777	same tuple. Convergence is non-trivial evidence: if the imscription were
4778	merely interpretive, independent derivations would diverge. When they
4779	converge, the tuple is not one analyst's reading of the system --- it
4780	is a finding about the system's type. The Hv1 channel
4781	distance-zero result (\Cref{sec:hv1}) was validated exactly this way:
4782	both channels were imscribed independently using only their known
4783	biophysical properties, and the convergence to $d = 0$ was not
4784	designed.
4785	
4786	Persistent \emph{non-convergence} on a specific primitive is itself
4787	informative: it signals that the system genuinely sits near a
4788	structural boundary in that dimension. In such cases, imscribe both
4789	brackets explicitly under distinct catalog names, compute their
4790	mutual distance and the tiers of their meet and join, and report
4791	the ambiguity as a structural finding rather than resolving it
4792	arbitrarily.
4793

4795	The inflaton has been re-imscribed three times as the grammar has
4796	developed; the current catalog entry (\texttt{inflaton}) and the
4797	in-paper imscription (\Cref{sec:cosmology}) differ on four primitives
4798	($d = 3.7283$), documenting a genuine shift in structural
4799	interpretation as the primitives were refined. The divergence is

\paragraph{Reproducibility: independent re-induction.}
The induction was performed a second time from scratch --- same
starting domain (CB[7] supramolecular chemistry), same methodological
sequence (orthogonality tests, diagonalization tests, delamination),
different language model session with no access to the first session's
output. The second session converged on a 12-axis formulation (the
Universal Constraint Propagation Tuple, UCPT) with different axis
labels: Structure, Interface Topology, Direction, Capacity,
Compatibility, Transformation, Self-reference, Polarity, Composition,
Context, Enforcement, Ordering. The count converged; the labels didn't.
Specifically, the UCPT's `Transformation' axis fused what the first
session delaminated into separate $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$ primitives, and the
`Ordering' axis had not yet separated into $\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$ (chirality/temporal
depth) and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ (winding number) --- the pre-delamination state the
Phase~2 tests are designed to correct. The convergence on twelve
structurally independent axes by two sessions with different labeling
conventions directly addresses the derivability question: if the count
were an artifact of the first session's representational choices, an
independent re-performance would not converge on the same cardinality.
The second induction session is available as supplementary
material~(\texttt{induction.txt}).

\paragraph{Cross-model induction array.}
To strengthen the reproducibility claim further, the same two-question

MoonshotAI), with no system prompt, no parameter constraints, and no
disclosure of the grammar or its cardinality. Each model received only

imscriptions in the resulting coordinate system. The proposed grammars
ranged from four to ten axes. At the four-axis extreme, one model
reduced all imscriptions to the integer tuple $S\langle q,\,s,\,n,\,p\rangle$
(charge, spin, chain length, polarity sign), arguing that ``any
yet-to-be-invented imscription is just a new set of four integers." At the
ten-axis extreme, a second model elaborated a Port-centric framework
with sub-dimensions for class, polarity role, multiplicity, geometry,
interaction strength, kinetic reversibility, selectivity signature, and
orthogonality --- an independent recovery of the grammar's $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont <}}$,
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊞}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$, $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$, and $\text{{\igprimfont >}}$ primitives, arrived at without
contact with the grammar. Intermediate sessions named between five and
seven axes, typically recovering a polarity or charge axis (mapping to
$\text{{\igprimfont <}}$), a directionality or geometry axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊣}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ⊢}}$), a
functional-outcome axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊙}}$), and a kinetic or
condition-sensitivity axis (mapping to $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$). These four dimensions
appeared across every session that proposed five or more axes. They're
the grammar's most redundantly encoded primitives.

No session reached twelve axes without applying the Phase~2 delamination
tests. This is the expected result: the tests exist precisely to separate
dimensions that are conflated at the vocabulary level --- kinetic and
sequential-logic aspects of $\text{{\igprimfont ⊤}}$ and $\text{{\igprimfont ∋}}$ appear as a single
`transformation' axis in most sessions before delamination, and
chirality and winding conflate into a single `ordering' axis before the
$\text{{\igprimfont ⊥}}$/$\text{{\igprimfont ⊡}}$ split. The array therefore replicates the \emph{pre-delamination
state} of the original induction: the grammar's structure is latent in
the chemistry literature vocabulary itself, and the Phase~2 tests are
the necessary precision instrument, not the generator of the structure.
The cross-model convergence on a structured tuple grammar --- spanning
radically different training corpora, architectures, and release
dates --- indicates that the imscription literature contains sufficient
co-occurrence structure to constrain an independent re-derivation of the
grammar's principal axes, regardless of the model performing the
induction.

\paragraph{Phase 3: validation.}
The twelve-primitive structure that resulted from Phases 1--2 was
validated by imscribing a benchmark for which the correct answer was
known: competitive displacement ordering in CB[7] host-guest
systems~\cite{kim2001,assaf2015}. Using only the ordinal rank of the
fidelity primitive $\text{{\igprimfont ⋈}}$ --- no binding energies, no computational
chemistry --- the algebra predicted the correct displacement ordering
six out of six times. This result wasn't designed in. It was the
evidential starting point for all subsequent cross-domain applications.

The grammar was extended, one domain at a time, by applying the same
iterative process: imscribe a class of systems, identify residuals that
the grammar handles incorrectly, test whether a missing primitive or a
misassigned coordinate is responsible, update, and re-validate.
No primitive was added after the initial twelve-step convergence.
